papers.abstract: The 2024 McDonald criteria broaden the definition of multiple sclerosis (MS), enabling diagnosis in individuals with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria. We assessed whether these criteria identify such cases using independent laboratory/imaging biomarkers and whether these biomarkers predict subsequent disease activity. Participants with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria were included and stratified according to the 2024 criteria. Serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) and 3T brain MRI measures-including normalised brain volumes, T2 lesion load (T2LL), cortical lesion (CL) and paramagnetic rim lesion (PRL)-were compared between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2024-negative groups, and with age/sex matched McDonald2017-positive cases according to the 2017 criteria; predictors of disease activity were assessed using penalised-Cox regression. A total of 141 participants were included: 95 not meeting the 2017 criteria (n = 64 asymptomatic MRI findings; n = 31 clinical presentations), stratified as McDonald2024-positive (n = 46) or McDonald2024-negative (n = 49), and 46 McDonald2017-positive cases. McDonald2024-positive vs. McDonald2024-negative cases showed higher age-corrected sNfL Z-scores (median 0.28[IQR 0.76] vs. -0.12[0.82], p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), reduced normalised thalamic volume (mean 0.009±[SD]0.0007 vs. 0.010 ± 0.0007, p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), and higher CL (1[4] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR < 0.001) and PRL (1[1] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR = 0.003) counts (differences remaining significant after age/sex, disease duration and T2LL adjustments). Biomarker profiles were comparable between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2017-positive cases. Penalised-Cox regression (n = 52) identified sNfL Z-score and PRL presence as the most consistently selected predictors of disease activity, with higher bootstrap stability for sNfL (0.84) than PRL (0.76), and good model discrimination (C-index = 0.71). The 2024 McDonald criteria identify individuals not meeting the 2017 criteria who already exhibit MS-like neuroinflammatory/neurodegenerative pathological changes. These are reflected by laboratory and imaging biomarkers, including sNfL, which may predict subsequent disease activity and complement current diagnostic frameworks to support early clinical decision-making. papers.abstract: Management of drug-resistant bacterial pneumonia has become increasingly precise, but early precision does not remove the need to reinterpret the patient's course during illness. Active and appropriate empirical therapy, informed by local epidemiology, remains essential, yet treatment often begins before the definitive microbiological profile is available or adequate drug exposure can be confirmed. While rapid diagnostics and pharmacological optimisation can narrow this initial uncertainty, the harder problem arises when antimicrobial treatment appears plausible but the patient shows delayed improvement, clinical deterioration, or incomplete recovery. These trajectories should not be treated as a single form of antibiotic failure. Instead, they require reassessment of whether the dominant limitation is persistent infection, inadequate drug exposure, dysregulated host response, a non-infectious mimic, or repair-limited recovery. In this Review, we propose a trajectory-guided conceptual framework that links management to the process most likely to limit recovery and distinguishes clinically implementable interventions from emerging translational concepts.

papers.abstract: Analysis of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation can enable noninvasive disease detection by leveraging tissue-specific epigenetic differences between malignant and nonmalignant cells. However, such analyses can be confounded by the repair of jagged DNA fragment ends during double-stranded sequencing library preparation, which introduces spurious methylation signals into cfDNA molecules. Here we present JEEPERS, a framework to detect and correct jagged-end-induced methylation errors while preserving duplex integrity and native methylation patterns. We showed high fidelity for measuring tumor burden and demonstrated allele-specific methylation differences at recurrent somatic mutations, revealing a link between adjacent CpG methylation and EGFR/TP53 driver and resistance mutations. We further demonstrated enhanced diagnostic performance across liquid biopsy applications, including tumor-type-specific methylation profiles, hemimethylation profiling, epigenetic-clock-based age estimation and cell type deconvolution. By faithfully correcting end-repair errors, JEEPERS provides a versatile framework for integrating mutations and methylation features in cfDNA at high resolution, enabling more precise molecular profiling and disease monitoring.

papers.abstract: Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1+ T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans. Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. This Tfh-microbiota-obesity pathway was also observed in diet-induced obese mice and in humans. Oral administration of IgA reduced Taurinivorans and alleviated adiposity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this axis. Tfh cell senescence impairs IgA production, disrupting gut microbial homeostasis, with consequences to host metabolic disease.

papers.abstract: After spinal cord injury, clinical management aims to support tissue perfusion, but current methods rely on the indirect control of arterial blood pressure without direct measurement of the local blood flow. This limits the ability to tailor drug delivery to the injured tissue. Here, we show that spinal cord blood flow can be regulated using a closed-loop controller that adjusts vasopressor infusion on the basis of real-time ultrasound flow measurement. We characterize the dynamic relationship between drug infusion, arterial pressure and spinal cord blood flow, and we use these data to design a feedback controller that targets a predefined flow level. We validate the system in simulations, implement the controller in real time in rodents and translate it to pigs. We show that the controller reduced blood flow deviations and variability compared with constant dosing and supported functional recovery in a rodent survival model. These results show a closed-loop spinal cord perfusion control strategy that leverages clinically available measurements and pharmacological interventions, supporting its translation to clinical settings for the management of acute spinal cord injury.

papers.abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

papers.abstract: Empirical and theoretical support is emerging for a view of macroevolution characterised by species' phenotypes tracking continually-moving adaptive peaks, interspersed with rare large shifts in the position of those peaks, likely corresponding to changes in species' adaptive zones. But we lack understanding of the factors that control these movements. We show in a sample of over 21,000 species from the five Vertebrate Classes (Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Amphibians) repeated convergence in the magnitude and frequencies of rare shifts in body-size peaks among species inhabiting the same dominant ecology. Peak-shifts (towards becoming larger or smaller) have been largest and most frequent among aquatic species, followed by terrestrial and then smallest and least frequent among volant species, independently of phylogenetic history. All peak-shifts are small in macroevolutionary time indicating that species in the terrestrial and aerial environments could have changed more had their environments favoured it. Within-population trait-variances from independent sources are largest in aquatic, followed by terrestrial then aerial species, consistent with evolution responding to differing macroevolutionary landscapes. Our results illustrate how ecologically varying adaptive landscapes have produced convergent outcomes of vertebrate macroevolution, giving rise to predictable evolutionary patterns even among species differing in fundamental aspects of development and thermoregulation.

papers.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

papers.abstract: Abstract The hyperactive kinase FLT3-ITD causes acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is a prognostic biomarker. We synthesized and characterized MA191 as a novel von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) E3 ubiquitin ligase-based proteolysis targeting chimera (PROTAC) for FLT3. MA191 induces apoptosis in cultured and primary AML patient cells harboring FLT3-ITD (IC 50 =9.6-11 nM; EC 50 =0.001-0.883 µM). Comparison with a VHL-binding-deficient stereoisomer of MA191 demonstrates that FLT3-ITD degradation is superior to kinase inhibition ( p < 0.03). Rapid depletion of FLT3-ITD by MA191 (DC 50 =10 nM) requires VHL, neddylation, proteasome activity, and the pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein BIM. MA191 reduces FLT3-ITD prior to apoptosis, uncovering apoptosis-independent roles of BIM for protein stability. Higher expression levels of FLT3 in leukemia cells than in healthy cells ( n = 3675/ n = 1249) are associated with worse AML patient survival ( p = 0.0099). MA191 does not harm healthy blood and bone marrow progenitor cells or myeloid cell differentiation. In Danio rerio larvae, MA191 halts AML cell proliferation without significant toxicity. Human stromal cell interactions and mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain of FLT3-ITD that confer resistance to FLT3 inhibitors do not abolish anti-leukemic effects of MA191. Accordingly, leukemia cells with acquired resistance to MA191 lack such mutations. We offer a framework for fast-acting next-generation FLT3 degraders that overcome resistance mechanisms to classical inhibitors.

papers.abstract: To elucidate the mechanisms underlying therapy-induced resistance, we investigated the temporal dynamics of the polyploid giant cancer cell (PGCC) life cycle following treatment with the microtubule-destabilizing agent vincristine (VCR). Longitudinal live-cell fluorescence imaging revealed that VCR-induced mitotic suppression activated a distinct PGCC life cycle characterized by nuclear amplification and progressive cellular reprogramming. At the cellular level, PGCCs entered a senescence-like state accompanied by an enhanced senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), increased epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), acquisition of early embryonic-like features, and multilineage differentiation potential into ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm. PGCC-derived progeny exhibited dose- and time-dependent changes in proliferative behavior, aggressive phenotypes in vitro, along with time-dependent tumorigenic potential in vivo. Remarkably, at the tissue level, PGCCs also underwent spatial nuclear reorganization and self-organization into morphologically defined glandular epithelial structures exhibiting varying degrees of tissue maturation, reminiscent of early embryonic development. Silencing IL1β, IL6, or IL8, or pharmacologically inhibiting their receptors, suppressed PGCC formation, budding, EMT, and embryonic-like reprogramming associated with tissue morphogenesis. Furthermore, NAMPT emerged as a key regulator of embryonic-like stemness, glandular morphogenesis, and structural expansion. Together, these findings reveal that therapeutic stress activates a PGCC life cycle capable of generating two divergent outcomes: resistant tumor regeneration through clonal selection of undifferentiated tumor cells and organized tissue differentiation through spatial nuclear reprogramming. Our study establishes a conceptual framework linking therapy-induced polyploidization, developmental plasticity, and resistance generation at both cellular and tissue levels.

In top tile analysis, model predictions for IDH1 were associated with immature leukemia phenotypes.

papers.abstract: The bone marrow microenvironment (BME) has a significant effect on bortezomib (BTZ)-based chemotherapy in patients with multiple myeloma (MM). However, how BME components drive effective BTZ-based chemotherapy to facilitate antitumor responses has yet to be fully understood. Using single-cell transcriptome analysis, we discerned a notable increase in the density of tumor-associated IL1B+ monocytes (TAMO_IL1B), a CD14+ monocyte subcluster, within the optimal responders (OR) group compared with the suboptimal responders (SOR) group. TAMO_IL1B in the OR group had significantly greater effects on the TGF-β signaling pathway. The ligand-receptor pair (THBS1-SDC1) interaction intensity in the THBS1 signaling pathway between TAMO_IL1B and tumor plasma cells (TPC) in the OR group was significantly greater than that in the SOR group. Furthermore, pseudotime trajectory analysis indicated that TAMO_IL1B predominantly occupied late differentiation stages and was associated with a favorable response within the OR group. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for TAMO_IL1B in shaping antitumor immunity. The THBS1-SDC1 axis may contribute to interactions between monocytes and plasma cells; however, functional validation is required before any therapeutic implications can be drawn.

papers.abstract: The immune checkpoints and their inhibitors are revolutionary advances in tumour immunotherapy. Immune checkpoints, however, have a broad spectrum effect. They not only contribute to tumour immune escape, but also are involved in the regulation of the pathopathological processes of numerous inflammatory illnesses, such as sepsis, autoimmune diseases, organ transplant rejection, and viral infections, among others. Today, a considerable gap in knowledge remains regarding immune checkpoints and immune checkpoint inhibitors in non-tumour inflammatory diseases, which remains largely unaddressed. At the same time, the emergence of immune-related adverse events and resistance challenges related to the clinical use of immune checkpoint inhibitors is becoming increasingly prominent, posing a significant obstacle to their application across various diseases. To overcome such issues, this narrative review establishes a systematic framework that links immune checkpoints to various inflammatory diseases and explores the associated therapeutic and clinical challenges. These diseases pose therapeutic and clinical challenges of immune checkpoint inhibitors, which we explore. The paper not only thoroughly describes the clinical picture, pathophysiology, and interventions in immunologic adverse events but also suggests a prospective strategy to confront the existing problems with immune checkpoint inhibitors in 3 dimensions: evaluation, management, and prevention. It will attempt to present a new conceptual framework for a comprehensive understanding of the dual role of immune checkpoints (in maintaining immune homeostasis and facilitating disease progression) and to provide a solid theoretical foundation for the development of safer and more effective cross-disease immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) is an aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, especially in relapsed/refractory patients. Aberrant PI3K/AKT/mTOR and NOTCH1 signaling converge on c-MYC to drive proliferation and ribosome biogenesis, but single-agent inhibitors targeting these pathways have shown limited clinical efficacy. An FDA-approved drug library screen identified osimertinib as a candidate anti-T-ALL agent. Its efficacy and mechanism were evaluated in four T-ALL cell lines (MOLT-4, Jurkat, CCRF/CEM, and MOLT-3) with different TP53 statuses and in primary T-ALL blasts. Combination studies with selinexor, an exportin 1 (XPO1) inhibitor, were performed. Multi-omics, biochemical, and functional assays were used, and efficacy and toxicity were assessed in T-ALL xenograft models. Osimertinib suppressed leukemic progression in vivo by promoting proteasome-dependent degradation of c-MYC through a non-canonical, EGFR-independent pathway that cannot be fully explained by inhibition of PI3K/AKT/mTOR or NOTCH1 signaling alone. This c-MYC suppression impaired ribosome biogenesis, and combining osimertinib with selinexor further disrupted this process. The combination increased apoptosis at low concentrations (0.5-2 µM osimertinib plus 20 nM selinexor), with clear synergy at 2 µM in all four T-ALL cell lines. Mechanistically, the combination caused nuclear retention of RPS6, nuclear accumulation of RPL5/RPL11, nucleolar stress (fibrillarin dispersal), decreased MDM2 protein levels, p53 stabilization, BAX activation (6A7), cytochrome c release, c-MYC depletion, and translational suppression. In vivo, the combination improved survival and reduced leukemic burden with minimal toxicity to normal cells at low doses. Potential biomarkers include c-MYC dependency and TP53 status as candidate stratification factors, and treatment-induced c-MYC depletion and RPL5/RPL11 nuclear accumulation as candidate pharmacodynamic biomarkers. Osimertinib plus selinexor depletes c-MYC, induces nucleolar stress, and suppresses translation, which together drive T-ALL cell apoptosis. This mechanism-driven combination shows preclinical efficacy with limited toxicity in the normal-cell and xenograft models tested. Further studies incorporating pharmacokinetic monitoring, PDX models, and prospective validation of candidate biomarkers such as c-MYC dependency, TP53 status, and RPL5/RPL11 nuclear accumulation are warranted before clinical translation.

papers.abstract: Solid tumors remain challenging for cellular immunotherapy, and CAR-T or CAR-M cells alone often have limited efficacy. Combining these approaches may improve therapeutic activity; however, our previous in vitro study observed increased IL-6, while extracellular matrix (ECM) barriers can restrict immune-cell access. We engineered IL6-CD147 CAR-M, a synthetic IL-6-responsive macrophage construct designed to couple an IL-6-binding scFv to a CD147-containing module. Following IL-6 stimulation, IL6-CD147 CAR-M showed increased MMP-2, MMP-9, MMP-11, and MMP-13 transcripts and proteins. A CD147-deletion control did not reproduce the enhanced MMP transcriptional response, and GM6001 reduced CAR-T cell migration through Matrigel toward IL6-CD147 CAR-M-conditioned medium. In defined 80:20 mixed-antigen tumor models, IL6-CD147 CAR-M plus CAR-T increased tumor killing and inflammatory/cytotoxic mediators while reducing detectable extracellular IL-6. In vivo, combined therapy reduced tumor burden, prolonged survival, increased immune-cell infiltration, altered immune composition, and was not associated with overt histopathological abnormalities in the examined major organs at the assessed time points. These findings support further evaluation of an IL-6-responsive, CD147-containing CAR-M strategy; proximal receptor signaling and the mechanism underlying reduced extracellular IL-6 remain unresolved.

papers.abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a well-established oncogenic driver in multiple solid tumors, most prominently in breast and gastric cancers. Beyond gene amplification-driven signaling through canonical PI3K/AKT and RAS/MAPK pathways, emerging evidence reveals that HER2 functions within a highly dynamic and context-dependent tumor ecosystem. Interactions between HER2-positive tumor cells and immune and stromal compartments actively shape the tumor microenvironment, contributing to immune evasion, therapeutic resistance and disease progression. A central challenge in the clinical management of HER2-altered cancers is pronounced spatial and temporal heterogeneity, which undermines both diagnostic accuracy and the durability of targeted therapies. In response, advances in multi-omics profiling, liquid biopsy technologies and artificial intelligence-assisted analytics are redefining HER2 assessment, shifting it from static tissue-based classification towards dynamic, minimally invasive monitoring. In parallel, the therapeutic landscape has evolved from single-agent HER2 blockade to rational combination strategies. In particular, antibody-drug conjugates have emerged as a transformative modality, extending the therapeutic reach of HER2 targeting beyond traditional indications and offering new opportunities to overcome heterogeneity and drug resistance. This review synthesizes current insights into the molecular and microenvironmental biology of HER2-altered solid tumors and discusses how these advances are reshaping next-generation precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Relapsed/refractory (R/R) lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a clinical challenge with limited therapies and poor prognosis. CAR‑NK cell therapy has shown promise in solid tumors, but its efficacy is limited by both the availability of effective targets and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. CD73 (NT5E), highly expressed across solid tumors, catalyzes adenosine production to drive immunosuppression, representing both a specific CAR‑NK target and a key leverage point to overcome tumor immune evasion. However, its systematic evaluation as a therapeutically actionable target for CAR‑NK cell therapy in R/R LUAD remains unexplored. We first characterized CD73 expression through integrative analysis of public datasets, primary and relapsed clinical LUAD specimens, and LUAD cell lines derived from primary and metastatic tumors. We then constructed CD73‑CAR‑NK cells and assessed their in vitro cytotoxicity across LUAD cell lines of varying malignancy, as well as their effects on extracellular adenosine and resistance to adenosine‑mediated immunosuppression. Finally, we assessed their antitumor efficacy in a stepwise manner across a tiered panel of in vivo models, including cell line‑derived xenograft (CDX), metastasis, patient‑derived xenograft (PDX), and clinically relevant immune‑humanized PDX models. CD73 expression was elevated in metastasis-derived LUAD cell lines and R/R LUAD specimens. Accordingly, CD73-CAR-NK92 cells exhibited potent cytotoxicity against CD73-high LUAD cells, accompanied by an activated effector phenotype, reduced extracellular adenosine, partial resistance to adenosine-mediated suppression, and limited activity toward normal bronchial epithelial cells. Notably, this enhanced function was consistently observed across multiple NK cell sources including peripheral blood-derived NK (PBNK), umbilical cord blood‑derived NK (UBNK), and iPSC-derived NK (iNK). In vivo, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, with enhanced tumor‑site enrichment, prolonged retention, and elevated intratumoral levels of TNF‑α and IFN‑γ. Importantly, in an immune‑humanized PDX mouse model, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly reduced the growth of R/R patient‑derived xenografts, accompanied by immune remodeling, without marked systemic inflammation during the observation period. These findings provide preclinical evidence that CD73-CAR-NK cells exhibit potent antitumor efficacy for R/R LUAD through their dual functions of eliminating CD73-high tumor cells and resisting adenosine-mediated immunosuppressive signaling, supporting their therapeutic potential.

papers.abstract: For more than a century after its initial description, glioblastoma (GBM) has remained one of the most therapeutically refractory human malignancies, resembling an almost impregnable fortress against modern oncology. Despite extensive molecular characterization and identification of numerous actionable targets, survival outcomes have improved only marginally. GBM is characterized by profound spatial and cellular heterogeneity, adaptive signaling rewiring, extensive phenotypic plasticity, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and major pharmacological constraints imposed by the blood-brain barrier. This review examines the resulting disconnect between biological rationale and clinical outcome through three interrelated translational principles that determine whether mechanistically compelling therapies can achieve meaningful clinical benefit in GBM. First, who is treated and what is biologically active: therapeutic efficacy depends on matching patients to functional pathway dependencies beyond static molecular alterations. Second, whether the drug reaches and modulates its intended target: candidate therapies must achieve sufficient intratumoral exposure and demonstrate target modulation. Third, how the tumor adapts under therapeutic pressure: durable efficacy requires accounting for receptor tyrosine kinase switching, phenotypic plasticity, immune adaptation, and spatial escape. By linking these principles to the molecular, spatial, and pharmacological organization of GBM, this review frames the disease as a dynamic tumor ecosystem and provides a framework for interpreting recurrent clinical failure and guiding more biologically informed therapeutic development.

papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer with somatic POLE exonuclease domain mutations (EDMs) has a highly favorable prognosis; however, the clinical implications of non-hotspot EDMs in POLE remain unclear. In 793 patients with endometrial cancer enrolled at the National Cancer Center and Juntendo University Hospitals, 25 prespecified variants were screened using the Luminex assay. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was carried out to evaluate 54 patients with hotspot and non-hotspot EDMs. In patients with endometrial cancer (n = 4864) registered in Genomics Evidence Neoplasia Information Exchange (GENIE), those harboring hotspot EDMs were matched with randomly sampled patients without EDMs, and a polymerase epsilon (POLE) score for gene panel testing was developed. In our cohort, POLE-EDMs, including hotspot (n = 91) and non-hotspot (n = 12) EDMs, were identified in 103 (12.9%) of 793 patients. The prevalence of grade 3 and advanced-stage endometrial cancer was higher in patients with non-hotspot EDMs than in those with hotspot EDMs. WES analysis of 54 patients revealed no significant differences in genomic mutations between the groups, and four non-hotspot EDMs were identified. A POLE-specific mutational signature was observed in tumors with EDM. In addition, the POLE score criteria were developed based on hotspot EDMs using the GENIE cohort, achieving a detection sensitivity of 0.94. Using the established POLE score, we identified nine non-hotspot EDMs. We identified 13 novel candidate non-hotspot EDMs using a newly established POLE score for gene panels and demonstrated an association between non-hotspot EDMs and favorable prognosis. The identification of additional non-hotspot EDMs will facilitate precise molecular classification of endometrial cancer.

papers.abstract: Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide and disproportionately affects older adults. As population ageing accelerates, the global cancer burden among older adults continues to increase. This study systematically evaluated the latest global cancer burden and its epidemiological characteristics among older adults. Data on the incidence and mortality of 33 malignancies, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, among adults aged 65 + were extracted from the Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024 and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 databases and stratified by age, sex, region, and Human Development Index (HDI). Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) were calculated. Annual percentage changes (APC) were used to characterize temporal trends. Decomposition analysis was performed to quantify the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological changes. Demographic projection methods and generalized additive model (GAM) were applied to forecast the cancer burden through 2050. In 2024, there were 9,966,392 new cancer cases and 6,001,290 cancer deaths among older adults worldwide, accounting for 51.11% and 61.84%, respectively, of all-age totals. Lung, colorectal, stomach, liver, and prostate cancers were leading causes of death. Incidence and mortality were higher in men and increased with age. The Western Pacific Region had the largest burden, whereas Europe Region had the highest ASIR. ASIR correlated positively with HDI (rs = 0.771), while mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) correlated negatively (rs = -0.825). From 2000 to 2023, ASIR and ASMR declined, although burden increased, primarily driven by population growth; pancreatic cancer exhibited the most rapid increase. Tobacco use remained the leading risk factor for mortality, while metabolic risks rose in importance. Under a demographic scenario assuming constant 2024 age-specific rates and changes only in population size and age structure, new cancer cases and deaths among older adults are projected to reach approximately 19.8 million and 12.5 million by 2050, roughly double the 2024 figures, with the largest increase in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Cancer burden in older adults is substantial, varying by sex, age, region, and development level. Precision prevention and control are urgently needed, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. papers.abstract: KRASG12D is a predominant driver in pancreatic cancer, yet the basis of intrinsic resistance to KRASG12D-targeted therapy remains poorly defined. Integrated genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics profiling across 242 patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and matched tumor tissues reveals a KRASG12D-mutant subset intrinsically resistant to KRASG12D-targeted therapeutics, characterized by marked downregulation of innate immune signaling pathways. Functional validation demonstrates that suppressing interferon signaling in sensitive models induces resistance, whereas activation of interferon signaling, particularly interferon beta (IFN-β), increases sensitivity in resistant models. Combining IFN-β with KRAS inhibitors (MRTX1133, HRS-4642, and RMC-6236) exhibits synergistic antitumor effects in intrinsically resistant pancreatic cancer. Mechanistically, sustained MYC activity is associated with attenuated sensitivity to KRAS inhibition and correlates with repressed interferon signaling, suggesting a potential role in promoting intrinsic resistance. These findings identify interferon signaling as a candidate determinant of KRAS-targeted therapy response and support interferon-based combinations as a potential strategy for intrinsically resistant pancreatic cancer.

papers.abstract: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

papers.abstract: Yersinia pestis (Y. pestis), the bacterial pathogen responsible for plague in humans, remains a public health threat, particularly in light of the recent emergence of antibiotic resistance strains. To better understand the immune response against plague and to identify potential targets for immunointervention, we performed an epitope mapping study of the IgG response against a library of peptides representing 18 Y. pestis proteins. The study included sera from 51 individuals who had recovered from plague, 26 uninfected human controls, and 20 sera from mice protected by a live-attenuated vaccine. Analysis of human sera revealed 32 reactive peptides distributed across eight protein antigens, whereas analysis of mouse sera identified 187 reactive peptides spanning all 18 proteins. Combined analysis of the human and mouse IgG responses to the 32 human-reactive peptides identified 27 B-cell epitopes located within YopD, YopB, LcrV, FyuA, Pla, Ail, Caf1, and PsaA. Of these, one epitope had previously been described as protective and another as immunodominant, whereas the remaining 25 represent immunodominant epitopes identified in this study. Interestingly, IgG antibody responses to selected YopD and YopB peptides were significantly stronger in pneumonic plague than in bubonic plague, suggesting that the distinct clinical manifestations of the disease may be associated with distinct underlying pathophysiological and molecular mechanisms. Our comprehensive mapping of linear IgG epitopes recognised by convalescent human sera, combined with prioritisation based on their predicted neutralising potential, provides a resource for future studies evaluating peptide-based diagnostics, vaccines, and monoclonal antibody therapies against plague. papers.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical notations, we detail their methodologies, explain key similarities and differences within and between categories, and summarize usage complexities. Given the diversity of methods, community benchmark datasets at single-cell resolution and careful sensitivity analyses are crucial for evaluating methods from multiple angles and potentially improving stability and generalizability. This article provides a basis for method benchmarking and highlights the remaining challenge of comparing methods for inferring pseudotime trajectories, RNA velocities, and cell potency.

papers.abstract: Upon infecting a bacterial cell, a lytic bacteriophage commandeers the host's resources to replicate, before lysing the cell to release new virions. As phages are obligate parasites, each stage of the infection process depends on the physiological parameters of the host cell. Given the inherent physiological variability within a population of genetically identical bacterial cells, we ask how the phage infection dynamic reflects such heterogeneity. Here, we introduce a time-lapse imaging assay for investigating the dynamics of individual infection steps by a single T7 phage on a single bacterium. This high-throughput, time-resolved assay enables us to monitor the infection progression simultaneously in multiple cells, uncovering substantial heterogeneity at each step and revealing correlations between infection dynamics and the physiological state of the infected cell. Simulations of competing phage populations reveal that heterogeneity in infection dynamics can significantly impact phage fitness, highlighting it as a potential evolutionary driver of phage-bacteria interactions. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

papers.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) enables scalable, label-free foundation models (FMs) that learn task-agnostic representations directly from images, bypassing cell segmentation and feature engineering inherent to classical morphological profiling. We present a large-scale evaluation of SSL FMs for image-based phenotypic profiling, covering contrastive (DINO), masked-based generative (MAE, iTPN) and hybrid (DINOv2) learning mechanisms, pretrained on all unannotated chemical perturbations from the Joint Undertaking for Morphological Profiling-Cell Painting (JUMP-CP) dataset (119,876 compounds, ~1.77 million images, 7 laboratories). Here we show that top-performing SSL models outperformed CellProfiler in compound-replicate retrieval on the held-out JUMP-Target2 set (302 annotated compounds, P ≤ 0.001). DINO and DINOv2 generalized across diverse perturbations and cell types, outperforming CellProfiler with 31-37% gains in site-averaged mean average precision for mechanism-of-action retrieval on EU-OPENSCREEN Bioactives (2,464 compounds), and consistently surpassing masked-based models across all benchmarks. This study provides a systematic assessment of SSL approaches for advancing morphological profiling and offers pretrained FMs to accelerate drug discovery.

papers.abstract: The clinical adoption of deep learning in pathology is largely hindered by the "black box" nature of current models, which often obscure the biological basis of prognosis. Here, we introduce MorphX, an interpretable framework that predicts patient survival by explicitly decoding multi-scale morphological patterns from whole-slide images. Unlike conventional methods relying on latent features, MorphX fuses macro-scale tissue texture with micro-scale nuclear metrics to attribute risk to interpretable biological phenotypes. In a multi-center study spanning 1,067 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), MorphX achieves concordance indices of 0.775-0.799 in discovery cohorts. Crucially, we derive eight distinct morphology-based biomarkers-driven by texture heterogeneity in necrotic regions, lymphocyte density, and nuclear shape-that demonstrate reproducible survival associations across independent cohorts, offering a granular resolution of tumor aggressiveness that transcends traditional histological grading. By translating opaque computational predictions into validated biological insights, MorphX supports trustworthy, transparent, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Host resistance to infection is initially determined by how well primed the innate immune system is to respond on first exposure to an invader, yet the mechanisms underlying this priming remain incompletely understood. Here we found that basal autophagy suppressed the expression of Il1a in alveolar macrophages (AMs) and an otherwise protective innate immune priming against Staphylococcus aureus and influenza A virus (IAV), independently of the microbiome and adaptive immunity. Inactivating autophagy genes in AMs led to elevated expression of IL-1α in AMs, which subsequently enhanced IL-1R-MyD88 signaling in neutrophils and increased the recruitment of myeloid cells to the lung. As a result, autophagy-deficient mice showed more efficient clearance of S. aureus along with reduced lung damage and inflammation. Similar to genetic inactivation of autophagy, overexpression of IL-1α in AMs conferred broad spectrum protection against S. aureus and IAV, suggesting a possible strategy to fine-tune immune responses to combat important respiratory infections.

papers.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.

papers.abstract: Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO2(101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene's reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.

papers.abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans, where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. We found that vaginal albumin concentrations are higher in women with recurrent VVC and during experimental VVC in mice. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans. This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans-induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC.

papers.abstract: Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity1-7, but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8) and Il1b. Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil-NLRP3-IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1+CD4+ T helper type 17 (TH17) cells9,10. After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung TH17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

Among patients meeting thresholds but not receiving transfusions intraoperatively, fewer than 15% required the corresponding product within 24 hours. Postoperative chest tube output was broadly similar across TEG-transfusion patterns, with no clear association between TEG concordance and early postoperative bleeding. Substantial discordance existed between manufacturer-derived post-bypass TEG thresholds and intraoperative transfusion practice. Transfusion appeared to reflect surgical complexity more closely than measured coagulation abnormalities.

papers.abstract: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.

papers.abstract: The systemic treatment landscape of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma has been transformed by immune-checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based regimens. These advances have led to efforts to combine ICIs with locoregional therapies (LRTs), particularly transarterial chemoembolization, transarterial radioembolization and external beam radiotherapy, in an attempt to improve tumour control and extend the benefits of ICIs to patients with intermediate-stage disease. The rationale for this combination approach is provided by the ability of LRTs to induce immunogenic cell death and tumour antigen release and to reprogramme the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Five phase III trials have thus far shown improvements in progression-free survival and objective response rates with regimens combining ICIs with transarterial chemoembolization. Early-phase and real-world data also support the combination of ICIs with transarterial radioembolization or external beam radiotherapy, particularly in selected patients with focal disease unsuitable for embolization or portal vein tumour thrombosis. However, various challenges remain, including patient selection and therapy sequencing, response assessment, and the growing difficulties in demonstrating survival advantages in the context of widespread post-progression crossover and effective subsequent therapies. In this Review, we describe the biological rationale, summarize the clinical evidence and discuss future directions for trial design, imaging and biomarker-driven patient selection in the integration of LRTs with immune-based regimens for patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.abstract: Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a subtype of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) and a rare, life-threatening complication of uncontrolled rheumatic diseases, characterized by systemic inflammation driven by aberrant activation of macrophages. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of plonmarlimab, a high-affinity neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), for the treatment of MAS. In this phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm clinical trial (NCT07034209 and CTR20230579), 18 patients with MAS secondary to systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease who were refractory to or had relapsed after high-dose glucocorticoid therapy were enrolled. Patients received plonmarlimab once weekly for 8 weeks at 6 mg/kg as the starting in the accelerated titration stage, and then at 10 mg/kg for the first two doses followed by dose adjustments at the investigator's discretion. The primary endpoint, overall response rate at week 8, was 83.3% (15/18) among all treated patients. The median time to response was 2.1 weeks (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.0-3.1), and the median time to remission of MAS symptoms was 1.1 weeks (95% CI, 1.0-2.3). The least-squares mean percentage reduction in glucocorticoid dose from baseline to week 8 was 79.3% (95% CI, 76.3-82.3), and 83.3% of patients (15/18) achieved a ≥ 50% reduction. No grade ≥ 3 infections were observed. Biomarker analysis showed rapid reductions in ferritin and interleukin (IL)-18 levels. Plonmarlimab showed promising clinical activity and was generally well tolerated in patients with MAS, and IL-18 may serve as a potential pharmacodynamic marker for GM-CSF antibody therapy.

papers.abstract: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8+ T cell activity, whereas CD8+ T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8+ T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

papers.abstract: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell-cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology.

papers.abstract: PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I-IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. Here we report the prespecified secondary endpoint, 5-year iDFS and exploratory circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) findings. After a median follow-up of 5.6 years, the 5-year iDFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 85.7 to 93.4) in group B (n = 267) and 92.4% (95% CI: 86.7 to 98.5) among 18F-FDG-PET responders achieving pCR without chemotherapy (n = 86), with one distant recurrence. The latter estimate describes a long-term outcome in a post-randomization subgroup defined by 18F-FDG-PET response and pCR and should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as causal effects of omitting chemotherapy. Detectable ctDNA at baseline or during treatment was associated with inferior iDFS, whereas ctDNA clearance correlated with higher pCR rates and improved long-term outcomes. These findings continue to support the clinical validity of an 18F-FDG-PET-guided, pCR-adapted approach and suggest a potential role for ctDNA in refining treatment individualization. papers.abstract: Despite decades of investigation, the fundamental molecular and cellular principles that enable bacteria to thrive within the tumor microenvironment have yet to be defined. Here, through a genome‑wide functional screen, we identify the bacterial genes and pathways that govern intratumoral fitness. Targeted deletion of nonglucose phosphotransferase systems to align bacterial metabolic preference with tumor metabolite availability promotes bacterial intratumoral fitness. Integrating multiple metabolic adaptations into a single tumor‑avid Escherichia coli strain (Ec‑TA) results in increased tumor colonization, not only after intratumoral delivery but also after intravenous delivery, leading to increased anti‑tumor efficacy when using Ec‑TA engineered to deliver an encoded immunostimulatory payload. Furthermore, Ec‑TA displaces wild‑type bacteria from pre‑colonized tumors when administered systemically, underscoring its potential for locally delivering therapeutics in the presence of resident tumor microbes. These data demonstrate that adapting bacteria to the unique characteristics of the tumor metabolic microenvironment can drive the development of safer and more effective chassis for next‑generation bacterial cancer therapies.

Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F1 was 0.72-0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min (P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01-2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff's α from 0.22-0.51 to 0.82-0.85).

Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Cardiovascular centers. Adults undergoing cardiac surgery. Remimazolam-based versus propofol-based general anesthesia for induction and maintenance. Fourteen reports describing randomized trials, including three theses, contributed 1,773 reported participants to the primary synthesis. All were conducted in China, and no key pooled result was supported exclusively by results at low risk of bias. One terminated European registry-results trial (23 treated patients) was included as supplementary sensitivity evidence. Data on major postoperative morbidity and mortality were too sparse to pool. Remimazolam was associated with fewer trial-defined intraoperative hypotension events (odds ratio [OR], 0.31; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20-0.47; p < 0.001; I² = 0%) and fewer bradycardia events (OR, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.12-0.34; p < 0.001; I² = 0%). It was also associated with shorter mechanical ventilation duration (mean difference [MD], -1.84 hours; 95% CI, -2.34 to -1.35 hours; p < 0.001; I² = 71%). Hospital length of stay crossed the line of no effect (MD, -0.48 days; 95% CI, -0.99 to 0.02 days; p = 0.06; I² = 37%). Certainty of evidence was very low for the hemodynamic and mechanical ventilation findings. Across the cardiac surgical populations represented in the included trials, remimazolam was associated with fewer trial-defined intraoperative hypotension and bradycardia events and shorter mechanical ventilation duration. The certainty of evidence for these associations was very low. The evidence does not establish improved major morbidity or mortality. Future multicenter confirmation is required.

papers.abstract: Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients and has been linked to poor outcomes and renal prognosis. Burn patients are particularly vulnerable, but the prognostic significance of dysnatremia in this population remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,758 burn patients admitted to a French burn center between 2011 and 2023. Dysnatremia was defined as at least one episode of hyponatremia ( 145 mmol/L) during intensive care unit (ICU) stay. The primary endpoint was the incidence of dysnatremia; secondary endpoints included major adverse kidney events (MAKE) at ICU discharge and acute kidney injury (AKI) occurrence and severity. Dysnatremia occurred in 56.3% of patients (n = 990), with hyponatremia in 50.5% (n = 888) and hypernatremia in 23.8% (n = 418). MAKE at ICU discharge did not differ between hyponatremic and normonatremic patients (12.6% vs. 10.9%, p = 0.304) but was sixfold higher with hypernatremia (32.3% vs. 5.4%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and burned total body surface area, hypernatremia was independently associated with MAKE at ICU discharge (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 4.03; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.92-5.56; p < 0.001), whereas hyponatremia was not (aHR 1.15; 95% CI: 0.85-1.55; p = 0.377). Clustering analysis identified three phenotypes: Cluster B (severe burns, worst outcomes), Cluster A (older patients, mostly hyponatremic, intermediate outcomes), and Cluster C (younger patients, mild burns, best outcomes). Dysnatremia affects over half of burn patients. Sodium disturbances should be viewed as markers of systemic severity, warranting close monitoring and preventive strategies.

papers.abstract: Fluid accumulation in surgical patients is associated with worse outcomes. Lung ultrasound (LUS) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading can assess congestion and thereby fluid tolerance. However, evidence regarding epidemiology, feasibility, and associations of reduced fluid tolerance with outcomes in surgical patients is lacking. This was a prospective single-centre observational cohort study in patients undergoing major gastrointestinal surgery. LUS and VExUS were performed before surgery and daily for up to 5 days after surgery. Reduced fluid tolerance was defined as pulmonary congestion (B profile on LUS), systemic congestion (VExUS ≥2), or both. The primary outcome was the prevalence of reduced fluid tolerance. Secondary outcomes were feasibility of ultrasound assessments, Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 complications, and length of stay (LOS). Of the 200 participants included, 73 (37%) exhibited signs of reduced fluid tolerance, most commonly on postoperative day 4 (n=28; 14%). Reduced fluid tolerance was primarily driven by pulmonary congestion (n=69; 95%), whereas systemic congestion was rare. In most affected patients (47 of 73; 64%), reduced fluid tolerance was limited to 1 day. Of 1200 planned assessments, 146 (12%) were missing: 123 because participants declined, mostly owing to the burden of repeated assessments, and 23 (2%) because of incomplete views. Reduced fluid tolerance was associated with LOS of >7 days (odds ratio 3.29; 95% CI 1.03-10.70), but not with major postoperative complications (hazard ratio 1.18; 95% CI 0.49-2.86). Reduced fluid tolerance detected by ultrasound is common after major gastrointestinal surgery and associated with increased LOS. Ultrasound assessments were technically feasible, but repeated assessments were perceived as a burden by a substantial proportion of patients. NCT06166719 (principal investigator: A.P.J. Vlaar; first registered: 04-12-2023).

papers.abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are integral components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of nearly every hallmark of cancer. Once viewed as a uniform, protumorigenic cell type, it is now clear that CAFs comprise a spectrum of dynamic and plastic functional states with both tumor-promoting and tumor-restraining capacities. This functional duality, conceptualized within the framework of cancer as a "wound that fails to heal", is dictated by their diverse cellular origins, the specific activation pathways engaged (such as TGF-β and PDGF), and the evolving cues from the TME. In this Review, we dissect the multifaceted roles of CAFs, from their promotion of cancer cell proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis through secreted factors and extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, to their profound influence on the immune landscape. We detail how distinct CAF subsets, such as myofibroblastic (myCAFs) and inflammatory (iCAFs) CAFs, orchestrate an immunosuppressive niche and contribute to therapeutic resistance. We also explore the compelling evidence for tumor-suppressive CAF functions, which have catalyzed a paradigm shift in therapeutic strategies-moving away from indiscriminate CAF ablation towards nuanced approaches aimed at reprogramming their state. These strategies include modulating key signaling pathways, normalizing the CAF-remodeled ECM, and exploiting unique metabolic vulnerabilities. Finally, we discuss how advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are resolving this complexity, paving the way for the development of precision therapies that can selectively neutralize pro-tumorigenic CAF activities while harnessing their beneficial functions to improve patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: To determine whether injection pressure and pressure-time characteristics can discriminate potentially hazardous needle-tip locations during peripheral nerve injection. Systematic review of experimental preclinical studies with narrative synthesis. Animal, ex vivo biological nerve, and human cadaver models of peripheral nerve injection. Needle placement and injection at intraneural, intrafascicular, perineural, or extraneural locations. CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 28, 2026 and updated on September 19, 2026. Studies reporting opening, peak, or plateau pressure or pressure-time characteristics in relation to anatomically defined needle-tip location were eligible. Human clinical studies and non-biological bench models were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using SYRCLE for animal studies and a domain-based framework for cadaveric studies. Because of substantial heterogeneity in experimental models, injection techniques, and pressure definitions, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria: 12 animal or animal ex vivo studies and 16 human cadaver studies. Intraneural injection was generally associated with higher peak and plateau pressures than perineural injection, but substantial overlap occurred across needle locations. Importantly, low pressure did not reliably rule out intraneural injection, while elevated pressure was also observed during needle-nerve contact and fascial injection. Consequently, the commonly proposed 15-psi threshold showed inconsistent sensitivity across experimental settings. Lower thresholds, including 12 psi, appeared more sensitive in some models but have not been clinically validated. Beyond absolute pressure values, the rate of pressure rise and pressure-time curve morphology showed potential for differentiating needle-tip locations. Injection pressure monitoring may provide a nonspecific warning of needle placement within or against a poorly compliant structure. However, preclinical evidence alone cannot establish whether it should be used routinely or whether it reduces nerve injury. No universal pressure threshold or clinically recommended injection rate can currently be defined.

papers.abstract: Propofol-based total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) is commonly used in neurovascular surgery, in which intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring limits inhalation anaesthetic use. However, propofol causes hypotension, and prolonged infusions can delay emergence. Remimazolam, a benzodiazepine whose effects are reversible with flumazenil, has been associated with less intraoperative hypotension than propofol, but its use raises concerns about postoperative delirium (POD). We tested whether remimazolam-based TIVA is noninferior to propofol-based TIVA for POD. In this single-centre, double-blind, randomised noninferiority trial, adults undergoing elective intracranial aneurysm clipping, arteriovenous malformation resection, microvascular decompression, or superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass received remimazolam-based TIVA with flumazenil reversal at emergence, or propofol-based TIVA, both with remifentanil. The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of POD within 5 days, assessed twice daily with the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for CAM-defined delirium (3D-CAM). The prespecified noninferiority margin was 10 percentage points. Among 686 patients in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, POD occurred in 44 of 344 (12.8%) with remimazolam and 37 of 342 (10.8%) with propofol (risk difference, 1.97 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.85 to 6.80; one-sided P<0.001 for noninferiority); per-protocol results were consistent. Hypotensive burden below a mean arterial pressure threshold of 65 mm Hg was lower in the remimazolam group (median, 0 vs 7.5 mm Hg min; P<0.001), and tracheal extubation in the operating room was more frequent (85.2% vs 67.3%). Remimazolam-based TIVA met the prespecified criterion for noninferiority to propofol-based TIVA with respect to postoperative delirium after elective neurovascular surgery. Interpretation should take into account that the observed incidence of postoperative delirium was lower than anticipated when the noninferiority margin was defined. NCT06115031 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

papers.abstract: Short-term peripheral nerve stimulation serves as a neuromodulation therapy that modulates neural activity to provide therapeutic benefit, particularly pain relief. This study investigated the effectiveness of short-term peripheral nerve stimulation as a minimally invasive approach for achieving pain relief. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from database inception till September 10, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults comparing short-term peripheral nerve stimulation with sham stimulation or usual care. The primary outcome was the change in average pain intensity during the implantation period. Eight RCTs (543 participants) were included. Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significant reductions in average pain intensity during the implantation period at 1-4 weeks (SMD = -0.48, 95% CI = -0.71 to -0.26, P < 0.0001) and 5-8 weeks (SMD = -0.96, 95% CI = -1.22 to -0.70, P < 0.0001), but no significant result after electrode removal. For worst pain intensity, the intervention group showed a greater reduction than the control group at all time periods except 1-4 weeks after EOT. Improvements in pain interference were delayed, becoming significant at 5-8 weeks during the implantation period (MD = -1.34, 95% CI = -1.86 to -0.82, P < 0.00001) and ≥8 weeks after the end of treatment (MD = -1.09, 95%CI = -1.69 to -0.50, P = 0.0003). Subgroup analyses showed improvements in postoperative pain. The usual care-controlled subgroup showed more pronounced and sustained benefits than the sham-controlled subgroup, and the chronic pain subgroup also showed more pronounced and sustained benefits compared to the acute/subacute pain subgroup. This meta-analysis provided preliminary evidence that short-term peripheral nerve stimulation may relieve pain during the implantation period, but not all outcomes suggest sustained improvements after electrode removal. papers.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia causes substantial morbidity, but tissue reservoirs that permit bacterial persistence remain poorly defined. Using intravenous USA300 MRSA infection in mice, multiplexed imaging, dual-species transcriptomics, host and bacterial genetics, and cell-based assays, we uncovered the renal inner medulla, the site of urine concentration, as an MRSA reservoir. In this hyperosmotic niche, MRSA evaded immune detection and co-opted tissue polyamines to sustain growth, enabling subsequent spread toward the renal cortex. Neutrophil recruitment to the inner medulla was profoundly delayed owing to osmotic inhibition of immune cell migration. Disruption of medullary osmolality with the loop diuretic furosemide accelerated neutrophil infiltration, limited bacterial spread, and improved renal outcomes. Mechanistically, polyamines promoted MRSA persistence through both extracellular and intracellular actions that depended on local osmolality and pH. In the medullary milieu, polyamines primarily associated with the bacterial surface and stabilized membranes against osmotic stress. Intracellular polyamines enhanced translation of guaB (inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase), the rate-limiting enzyme in bacterial de novo purine biosynthesis. The polyamine-catabolizing gene speG (spermidine acetyltransferase), uniquely present in epidemic USA300 MRSA strains, mitigated polyamine toxicity and conferred a selective advantage in the polyamine-rich kidney. These findings revealed the inner medulla as a physiologically immune-restricted MRSA reservoir and supported modulation of medullary osmolality and bacterial polyamine metabolism as candidate adjunctive strategies for limiting renal persistence and dissemination during MRSA bacteremia.

papers.abstract: To characterize clinicopathologic, treatment-related, and sociodemographic factors associated with rapid versus late relapse in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), and to evaluate how relapse timing influences metastatic patterns and survival outcomes. Using linked Swedish population-based registers, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of women diagnosed with non-metastatic TNBC between 2007 and 2021. Patients were classified into three groups based on time to distant relapse or death: rapid relapse (rrTNBC; ≤24 months), late relapse (lrTNBC; >24 months), or event-free at last follow-up. Tumor characteristics, comorbidity, treatments, and sociodemographic variables were compared across groups. Multivariable logistic regression and survival outcomes were assessed. Sensitivity analyses restricted to healthcare regions with complete relapse data were performed. Among 8,298 patients, 15% experienced rrTNBC, 18% lrTNBC, and 67% remained event-free. rrTNBC was associated with older age, larger tumors, nodal involvement, advanced stage, and a higher frequency of visceral and multi-organ metastases. Patients with rrTNBC were less likely to receive adjuvant systemic therapy or radiotherapy and more likely to undergo mastectomy. Sociodemographic disparities were observed, with rrTNBC more frequent among patients who were single or widowed, lower educated, or had lower household income. Survival outcomes were substantially worse for rrTNBC compared with lrTNBC and event-free patients. Rapid relapse defines a particularly vulnerable TNBC population characterized by aggressive tumor biology, early dissemination, inferior survival, and sociodemographic disadvantage, while lrTNBC represents an intermediate phenotype with delayed disease progression. Distinguishing rrTNBC from lrTNBC may improve risk stratification, guide treatment decisions, and support more personalized follow-up strategies.
