papers.abstract: Cancer surgical research is essential to discover newer treatment options, enhance survival, improve quality of care, and more importantly, impede the rising global cancer burden. The inability to conduct cancer surgical research can have detrimental health and economic effects at the individual and societal levels. It is well known that there are several barriers to conducting cancer surgical research, and these barriers are exacerbated in low-resource settings. The second Lancet Oncology Commission on Global Cancer Surgery Action on research helps to address these barriers and outline strategies that promote cancer surgical research on the global stage. This study used the principles of Implementation Science taken from the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to help develop the content and increase the likelihood of success in implementing the recommendations in this Action. The Annals of Surgical Oncology Series on the second Lancet Oncology Commission on Global Cancer Surgery hopes to enhance the visibility of the eight critical Actions within this important Commission to the primary stakeholders, the surgeons. The authors hope this Action on research will help to address these barriers and implement resource-stratified solutions to build individual, institutional, and system-wide capacity for cancer surgical research. These efforts should lead to the development of a robust cancer surgical research infrastructure that will eventually translate to improved patient and population outcomes.

papers.abstract: Innovation in surgical oncology is developing rapidly, and new therapies and technologies have expanded across academic centers, integrated networks, and community sites, at times outpacing the evidence, expertise, and necessary infrastructure. Although innovation is essential to our field's progress, patient safety and demonstrated efficacy must remain paramount. Adopting specialized or understudied approaches without appropriate guardrails risks patient harm and generates low-quality, confusing evidence that impedes progress for future patients with cancer. To provide structured, practical guidance on this challenge to our field, the Society of Surgical Oncology Quality Committee recommends application of the IDEAL framework for surgical innovation, which organizes the life cycle of new procedures, programs, and technologies into five stages: idea (stage 1), development (stage 2a), exploration (stage 2b), assessment (stage 3), and long-term study (stage 4). Using expert consensus, we illustrate this IDEAL-informed approach with four examples that represent the breadth of the current implementation landscape in surgical oncology: hepatic artery infusion pump chemotherapy, robotic nipple-sparing mastectomy, histotripsy, and artificial intelligence. These technologies are used as concrete illustrations of principle, not as the primary subject of this statement. The central tenant is this: before any program or technology is broadly taken to the bedside, there must be evidence to support its efficacy. The recommendations described in this report have been endorsed by the Society of Surgical Oncology.

papers.abstract: Health literacy, physical activity, and complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) are increasingly recognized as important factors influencing coping strategies, quality of life, and well-being in cancer patients. However, empirical evidence on their interrelationships remains limited. We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional study between April and November 2024 at one Comprehensive Cancer Center and eleven oncological sites across Germany. A total of 316 cancer patients completed a standardized questionnaire assessing health literacy, self-reported sport participation, expectations toward physical activity, affective attitudes toward physical activity, CAM use, spirituality, nutrition, and life satisfaction. Descriptive statistics, reliability analyses, t-tests, and Spearman's correlations were performed. Among the 316 participants, health literacy (M = 3.10, SD = 0.44) and life satisfaction (M = 7.03, SD = 2.02) were high. Health literacy did not differ significantly by self-reported pre-diagnosis sport participation. Life satisfaction likewise did not differ by self-reported pre-diagnosis sport participation. In contrast, more positive affective attitudes toward physical activity were significantly correlated with health-related expectations toward physical activity (r = 0.580, p < 0.001), body-related motives (r = 0.471, p < 0.001), and life satisfaction (r = 0.212, p < 0.001). CAM use was frequent, with 44.9% reporting vitamin D supplementation and 37.5% other vitamins or dietary supplements. While self-reported sport participation did not show significant associations with life satisfaction, motivational and cognitive factors-such as positive attitudes and expectations-were linked to health literacy and well-being. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening patient-centered communication, motivational counseling, and health literacy as key elements of integrative oncology.

papers.abstract: The Siglec-sialoglycan axis is an emerging glyco-immune checkpoint in cancer. This is supported by the frequent upregulation of both Siglecs and sialoglycans in the tumor microenvironment. Siglecs are receptors expressed on immune cells that recognize sialoglycans, carbohydrate structures terminated by sialic acid. Most Siglec receptor family members are inhibitory and suppress immune cell activation through the recruitment of SHP-1 and SHP-2 phosphatases. It is well established that Siglecs expressed by immune cells bind ligands present on other cells, including tumor and stromal cells (trans-interactions). However, immune cells themselves also express sialoglycans that can serve as ligands for Siglecs on the same cell surface (cis-interactions). Over the past two decades, numerous studies have addressed how Siglec trans-engagement facilitates immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment. The role of cis-interactions in regulating Siglec function and their impact on immune cell activity, however, remains an underexplored topic for most Siglec family members. This review discusses how cis-ligands modulate Siglec function, the mechanisms regulating sialic acid expression on immune cell surfaces, and the functional relevance of cis-interactions expressed by immune cells in the tumor microenvironment. A better understanding of these processes may facilitate the development of next-generation therapeutics targeting the Siglec-sialoglycan axis in cancer.

papers.abstract: Alterations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) pathway, particularly FGFR3, are among the most common genomic events in urothelial carcinoma (UC) and represent a cornerstone of precision oncology. Although FGFR3 alterations predominate, selected FGFR2 fusions also identify patients who may benefit from targeted therapy. This review summarizes the biology, molecular diagnostics, and evolving clinical applications of FGFR alterations in UC. FGFR2/3 alterations are clinically actionable biomarkers across non-muscle-invasive, muscle-invasive, metastatic, and upper-tract UC. Comprehensive genomic profiling, tissue sequencing, plasma circulating tumor DNA, urine-based molecular assays, and molecular residual disease assessment are expanding their roles in diagnosis, treatment selection, surveillance, and disease monitoring. Recent clinical studies support combination strategies, next-generation FGFR inhibitors, and earlier use of FGFR-directed therapy, while emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-assisted pathology and integrated multi-omic biomarkers, may further improve patient selection. FGFR alterations have become integral to the molecular classification and precision management of UC. Continued advances in molecular diagnostics, liquid biopsy, biomarker-guided therapy, and next-generation FGFR inhibitors are expected to further personalize care. This review provides a practical framework for integrating FGFR biomarkers into contemporary management and highlights emerging developments likely to influence future clinical practice.

papers.abstract: Primary bone cancers include multiple histologic types, with survival differing by age and location. Results from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 were analyzed to support policies and initiatives worldwide. To estimate the global burden of bone cancer from 1990 to 2023 and forecast future trends to 2050. This systematic analysis estimated bone cancer incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in 204 countries and territories grouped by GBD super-regions and World Bank income groups from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts through 2050. Individuals of all ages with bone cancers included in the GBD 2023 study were included in analyses. Data were analyzed from June 2023 to July 2025. The GBD 2023 study used standardized estimation methods to describe bone cancer incidence, mortality, and DALYs in 2023, as well as trends over the past 3 decades and forecasts through 2050. All estimates are presented with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), and age-standardized rates (ASRs) were calculated using GBD-specific age weights. In 2023, there were 111 000 (95% UI, 81 300-164 000) malignant bone cancer cases, 76 600 (95% UI, 60 700-96 300) deaths, and 3.02 million (95% UI, 2.29 million-3.96 million) DALYs globally. A bimodal age distribution was noted in both incidence (peaking at ages 10 to 14 years and 65 to 69 years) and mortality (peaking at ages 15 to 19 years and 65 to 69 years). The highest ASRs for incidence were in Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania (1.6 per 100 000; 95% UI, 1.1-2.4), while Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest ASRs for DALYs (51.0 per 100 000; 95% UI, 27.7-79.7). By World Bank income group, upper-middle-income countries had the highest ASRs for incidence, whereas low-income countries exhibited the highest ASRs for both mortality and DALYs. Globally, incident cases, deaths, and DALYs increased from 1990 to 2023, while global mortality and DALY ASRs were relatively stable; high-income countries experienced a decline in mortality and DALY ASRs. Forecasts suggest a potential increase in global cases and deaths by 2050. In this systematic analysis, the burden of bone cancer varied by age, geography, and time, underscoring global disparities. These findings provide valuable insights to inform health system planning and resource allocation tailored to different settings.

papers.abstract: Consolidation immunotherapy improves outcomes after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Disease progression remains common, and more effective consolidation strategies are needed. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of benmelstobart with or without anlotinib as consolidation therapy after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC. This multicenter double-blind phase 3 randomized clinical trial took place at 42 centers in China from 2020 to 2023 among patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy. In stage 1, patients were randomized 1:1:1 to 2 active regimens or placebo; in stage 2, additional patients were randomized 1:1 between the active regimens to power their direct comparison. Data cutoffs were November 30, 2023, for stage 1 and July 8, 2024, for the pooled analysis. Data analysis was performed from January 17 to March 23, 2025. Patients were randomized to receive benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart plus anlotinib placebo, or their matching placebos. Primary end point was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). Of 553 participants (median [IQR] age, 62 [56-67] years; 495 male individuals [89.5%]), 390 were randomized in stage 1 and 163 in stage 2. In stage 1, median PFS was 15.1 months (95% CI, 9.4-21.7) with benmelstobart plus anlotinib, 9.7 months (95% CI, 6.0-34.4) with benmelstobart alone, and 4.2 months (95% CI, 3.2-6.8) with placebo. The hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.49 (95% CI, 0.36-0.66; P < .001) for benmelstobart plus anlotinib vs placebo and 0.53 (95% CI, 0.39-0.72; P < .001) for benmelstobart vs placebo. In the pooled stage 1 and 2 analysis, median PFS was 17.4 (95% CI, 12.5-24.8) months with benmelstobart plus anlotinib and 11.2 (95% CI, 7.0-20.7) months with benmelstobart alone (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.63-1.08; P = .12). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 48.8%, 29.4%, and 19.7% in the benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart alone, and placebo groups, respectively; grade 5 events occurred in 7.2%, 1.4%, and 1.5%, respectively. This randomized clinical trial found that benmelstobart with or without anlotinib significantly improved PFS compared with placebo. Adding anlotinib did not significantly improve PFS compared with benmelstobart alone and increased severe and fatal treatment-related adverse events. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04325763.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate whether voxel-level IVIM-based habitat analysis supports exploratory pretreatment stratification of Ki-67 proliferation status in cervical cancer. Between January 2019 and June 2025, medical records of 149 patients with histopathologically confirmed cervical cancer were initially screened. Before image-quality assessment, 49 were excluded because IVIM MRI had been performed after chemoradiotherapy (n = 5), cervical biopsy sampling (n = 21), or lesion excision (n = 10), or because no pathological Ki-67 immunohistochemistry result was available (n = 13). Of the remaining 100 patients, 17 were excluded because of severe image artefacts (n = 11) or lesions too small for reliable ROI delineation (n = 6), leaving 83 patients for analysis. Patients were stratified into high Ki-67 (Ki-67 >70%, n = 38) and low/equal Ki-67 (Ki-67 ≤70%, n = 45) groups. Solid-tumour regions were analysed with patient-level K-means clustering using normalised D, f, and ADC features; D* was excluded from clustering because of voxel-level fitting instability. Habitat labels were harmonised according to quantitative parameter profiles and treated as image-defined phenotypes. Habitat-derived features, conventional ROI parameters, and logistic models were evaluated for Ki-67 stratification. Hab1 ADC was lower in the high- than in the low/equal-Ki-67 group (median [Q1-Q3], 0.947 [0.862-1.161] vs. 1.257 [1.113-1.455] × 10-3 mm2/s; P < 0.001; BH q = 2.04×10-6), whereas Hab3 volume proportion was higher (0.396 [0.341-0.488] vs. 0.279 [0.190-0.390]; P = 0.002; BH q = 0.006). Hab1 ADC outperformed conventional ROI ADC for identifying high Ki-67 status [AUC, 0.826 (95% CI, 0.726-0.909) vs. 0.563 (95% CI, 0.429-0.695); paired DeLong P < 0.001]. The combined Hab1 ADC and Hab3 volume proportion model showed the numerically highest discrimination (apparent AUC, 0.877; 95% CI, 0.794-0.938), but this numerical improvement over Hab1 ADC alone was not statistically significant (paired DeLong P = 0.056). Fixed-feature leave-one-out validation of the combined model yielded an AUC of 0.855 (95% CI, 0.771-0.923) and a Brier score of 0.157 (95% CI, 0.112-0.204). IVIM-based habitat analysis showed exploratory potential for non-invasive Ki-67 stratification by isolating a low-diffusivity imaging compartment otherwise obscured by conventional whole-tumour averaging. The combined habitat model should be interpreted as a research-stage imaging biomarker, not a clinical decision tool, and requires prospective external validation before clinical translation.

papers.abstract: Tumor budding (TB) is a histopathological marker of tumor aggressiveness and an established prognostic factor in colorectal cancer. In rectal cancer, however, TB is usually assessed on biopsy or resection material, and a reliable result may not be available when preoperative management is being considered. To develop and internally validate a radiomics model for preoperative discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB in patients with rectal cancer who proceed to upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC, with alternative feature sets and algorithms evaluated exploratorily. This retrospective study included 139 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who had received no neoadjuvant treatment. TB was assessed on postoperative resection specimens. T1WI, T2WI, arterial-phase contrast-enhanced T1WI, and DWI were analyzed. Radiomics features were extracted from the tumor core, a combined tumor-plus-2-mm expansion, and an isolated external 2-mm ring. Seven feature sets and four machine-learning algorithms were evaluated; the primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC. Feature filtering, imputation, selection, and scaling were performed within the training portion of every split. Model performance was estimated using stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated five times and patient-level out-of-fold (OOF) probabilities. The primary core-ROI Elastic Net model achieved a repeated cross-validation AUC of 0.825 (range 0.809-0.839 across repetitions), with PR-AUC 0.781, sensitivity 0.604, specificity 0.851, and Brier score 0.173. Its patient-level mean OOF AUC was 0.829 (2,000 paired bootstrap replicates; 95% CI, 0.755-0.896). At a probability threshold of 0.50, patient-level sensitivity was 0.607 and specificity was 0.867. In conditional paired bootstrap comparisons, the core model showed higher AUCs than the clinical, peritumoral-ring, clinical-plus-expanded, clinical-plus-core, and clinical-plus-core-plus-ring models (BH-adjusted P = 0.004-0.005). The difference versus the expanded ROI was smaller and did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (P = 0.052). Multiparametric MRI radiomics features from the tumor core showed promising internal discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB among patients who underwent upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The model may support preoperative TB risk stratification in this population, but external validation is required before clinical use.

papers.abstract: Adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer survivors have complex long-term survivorship needs beyond cancer recurrence surveillance. Although survivor concerns and healthcare provider perspectives have been reported separately, few studies have evaluated both within the same healthcare setting. We conducted complementary surveys of AYA cancer survivors and physicians to characterize survivorship concerns, barriers to long-term follow-up (LTFU), and telemedicine preferences. This single-center, cross-sectional study included questionnaire surveys of 98 AYA cancer survivors receiving outpatient follow-up after cancer treatment and 45 physicians involved in AYA survivorship care at the National Cancer Center Hospital, Japan. Survivors were surveyed regarding LTFU, survivorship concerns, and telemedicine preferences, and physicians regarding LTFU practices, referral barriers, and AYA-specific challenges. Associations between survivor characteristics and telemedicine preference were explored using univariable analyses. Among survivors, 84 of 98 (85.7%) considered LTFU necessary, and 51 (52.0%) reported difficulty attending follow-up because of school or work commitments. Of 91 survivors evaluable for telemedicine preference, 69 (75.8%) were likely or somewhat likely to use at least one telemedicine service. Among all 98 survivors, frequently selected telemedicine topics included disease information (45.9%), daily activities (31.6%), anxiety and worry (30.6% each), financial issues (29.6%), and work- or school-related concerns (27.6%). No demographic, clinical, treatment-related or healthcare utilization factors were significantly associated with telemedicine preference. Among physicians, 13 of 44 (29.5%) reported an established departmental LTFU policy. Follow-up at the treating cancer center was supported by 76.2% for survivors at high risk of recurrence but by only 21.4% for all AYA survivors. Major barriers to coordinated care included difficulty identifying hospitals providing cancer-specific LTFU (73.8%) or multidisciplinary care (71.4%). Physicians identified reproductive medicine and life events as major AYA-specific challenges and mental health, endocrine disorders, and sexual and reproductive health as areas requiring additional support. AYA cancer survivors reported substantial survivorship concerns, whereas physicians identified barriers to coordinated multidisciplinary care. Telemedicine was of interest to many survivors and warrants prospective evaluation as a potential component of multidisciplinary survivorship care.

papers.abstract: Bone disease is a common manifestation of multiple myeloma. Although anti-resorptive therapy is recommended by guidelines, implementation can be variable. We sought to evaluate practice patterns for myeloma bone disease management and to identify opportunities for harmonization. An online survey was distributed to clinicians who see patients with multiple myeloma at medical centers affiliated with the Big Ten Cancer Research Consortium. Anonymous responses were collected regarding self-reported demographics, as well as practice patterns regarding preferred antiresorptive agent, dosing, duration of therapy, therapy modifications, vitamin and mineral supplementation, dental restrictions, and management at relapse. A total of 100 responses were collected from 11 different academic institutions and their community-affiliated sites. Respondents were predominantly physicians (74%) working in an academic setting (77%), with variable time practicing independently and number of myeloma patients seen per year. Most respondents (89%) reported using zoledronic acid as the preferred agent, with every 4 weeks as the most common frequency (for zoledronic acid 70%, denosumab 64%), with most administering therapy for 2 years (72%). Most clinical scenarios did not affect anti-resorptive choice at diagnosis, except for severe renal insufficiency. Dental recommendations were heterogeneous. There was low utilization of biomarkers to guide management decisions. Our survey suggests that at the time of diagnosis, most clinicians administer appropriate supportive care for myeloma bone disease. Further study is needed to help unify practice patterns in the relapsed setting, when dental care is suboptimal, and when it is appropriate to tailor such therapy.

papers.abstract: Residual cancer burden (RCB) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) provides prognostic information, but its combination with immune microenvironment features for recurrence prediction remains underexplored. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 420 consecutive patients with breast cancer who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by definitive surgery between January 2015 and June 2024. Residual cancer burden (RCB) and post-neoadjuvant immune features, including tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), CD8, FOXP3, and the proportion of CD163-positive among CD68-positive macrophages, were assessed. Patients were stratified by calendar era and randomly partitioned within strata into a training cohort (n=294) and an internal hold-out validation cohort (n=126). A LASSO-penalized Cox workflow was used for predictor selection, followed by unpenalized Cox refitting. Model performance was evaluated using C-statistics, time-specific Brier scores, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and 5-year time-dependent decision curve analysis. During a median follow-up of 61 months, 126 first recurrence events were observed (88 training and 38 validation). The final combined model retained RCB category, triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), CD8 status, and CD163-positive macrophage proportion. The combined model achieved C-statistics of 0.79 (95% CI 0.75-0.83) in the training cohort and 0.75 (95% CI 0.69-0.81) in the internal validation cohort, with corresponding 5-year Brier scores of 0.142 and 0.158. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected C-statistic of 0.772 and calibration slope of 0.92. The combined model provided the greatest net benefit among the evaluated models over 5-year threshold probabilities of approximately 15%-45%. Integration of RCB with TNBC status and post-neoadjuvant CD8 and CD163-positive macrophage features may provide incremental prognostic information for recurrence after neoadjuvant therapy. The model showed acceptable internal discrimination and calibration, but external validation is required before clinical implementation or treatment-directed use.

papers.abstract: Primary enteric-type adenocarcinoma of the renal parenchyma is an exceptionally rare malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of renal epithelial tumors. Due to its morphological and immunohistochemical overlap with metastatic gastrointestinal malignancy, establishing a primary renal origin presents a considerable diagnostic challenge. Radical nephroureterectomy has traditionally been the standard surgical treatment. We report a 47-year-old asymptomatic female with an incidental 68 mm cystic-solid left renal mass detected during a trauma evaluation. Imaging suggested Bosniak category IV on computed tomography and cystic teratoma on magnetic resonance imaging. Notably, the patient had bilateral renal malrotation. Serum tumor markers (CEA and CA19-9) were within normal limits. The patient underwent successful robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy with a warm ischemia time of 15 minutes. Histopathology revealed adenocarcinoma with an enteric immunophenotype: positive for CK20, CDX-2, SATB2, and Villin, with complete loss of PAX-8 and GATA-3. Postoperative gastrointestinal endoscopy and 18F-FDG PET-CT excluded primary gastrointestinal or distant occult malignancies, confirming a primary renal parenchymal origin. At one-month follow-up, the patient showed no evidence of recurrence without adjuvant therapy. This case represents the first reported association of primary enteric-type renal adenocarcinoma with bilateral renal malrotation and demonstrates that robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy can be a feasible nephron-sparing approach for selected patients with this aggressive tumor. A systematic diagnostic approach including surgical resection, immunohistochemical profiling, and exclusion of gastrointestinal metastasis is essential for accurate diagnosis and optimal management.

papers.abstract: Soft tissue sarcoma (STS) is a rare but aggressive mesenchymal malignancy that accounts for less than 1% of all adult cancers. Head and neck soft tissue sarcomas (HNSTS) are infrequent malignant tumors arising from mesenchymal and neuroectodermal tissues in the head and neck region with a poor prognosis, and recurrence is predominantly local. There are few targeted management guidelines. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman with postoperative recurrence of HNSTS. The patient was diagnosed with high-grade soft tissue sarcoma of the scalp in February 2025 and treated with surgery. In June 2025, the patient was diagnosed with recurrence, and was subsequently treated with combination therapy consisting of the anti-angiogenic inhibitor anlotinib and radiotherapy. In December 2025, after nine cycles, the patient showed a complete response (CR) to therapy. This indicates that radiotherapy combined with anti-angiogenic targeted therapy may produce synergistic effects in patients with HNSTS and provide directions for future clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) changes for treatment response in colorectal cancer(CRC) patients receiving CAPOX chemotherapy, providing a reliable indicator for clinical efficacy monitoring. Clinical data of CRC patients who first received the CAPOX regimen at the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University between January 1, 2016 and January 31, 2026 were retrospectively collected. Parameters included operation date, chemotherapy administration dates, disease progression (PD) time, preoperative CEA, baseline CEA before chemotherapy, CEA before each cycle, and CEA within three months post-chemotherapy. Disease-free survival (DFS) was calculated. Patients were divided into Group 1: CEA is in the normal range (all values are ≤ 5ng/ml); Group 2: Decreasing or normalization type (not Group 1, and the last valid value ≤ 5ng/ml, or a decrease of ≥20% compared to the individual's previous peak); Group 3: Persistent or new-onset abnormal type (the rest, that is, the last value > 5 and the decrease from the peak value < 20%). Survival curves were plotted using the Kaplan-Meier method, and multivariate Cox regression was used to assess correlations between CEA changes, treatment efficacy, and DFS. Median DFS (mDFS) was 55.668 months (95% CI: 51.511-58.826) in Group 1 (n=84); 42.271 months (95% CI: 35.438-49.104) in Group 2 (n=47) and 19.980 months (95% CI: 11.198-28.762) in Group 3 (n=11). Dynamic changes in serum CEA have good predictive value for the efficacy of CAPOX chemotherapy in CRC. This predictive value is primarily significant in TNM Stage III patients and serve as an independent prognostic factor. Patients with decreased or persistently normal CEA levels have a better prognosis.

papers.abstract: The malignant transformation of endometriosis has garnered widespread attention; however, most cases of malignant transformation occur in ovarian endometriomas, while extraovarian malignant transformation is rare. We present an uncommon instance of extraovarian endometrioid adenocarcinoma originating from the uterosacral ligament(USL) in a 41-year-old female, which emerged from deep infiltrating endometriosis of the uterosacral ligament 4 years after a previous clinical diagnosis of adenomyosis. A 41-year-old woman, presenting with progressively worsening secondary dysmenorrhea for 4 years and dyspareunia for over 1 year, underwent "laparoscopic total hysterectomy, left adnexectomy, right salpingectomy, right ovarian endometrioma cystectomy, bilateral uterosacral ligament DIE lesion resection, anterior rectal resection, rectal DIE lesion resection with end-to-end anastomosis, left ureteral DIE lesion excision, and pelvic adhesiolysis." Postoperative pathology revealed a well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the uterosacral ligament (FIGO grade 1), arising from malignant transformation of pelvic endometriosis. Subsequently, a completion surgery was performed, consisting of "transabdominal right oophorectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy, omentectomy, biopsy of an ileal surface lesion, resection of a right pelvic wall peritoneal lesion, and pelvic adhesiolysis." Postoperative pathological examination revealed a metastatic carcinoma in the right obturator lymph node. The final diagnosis was stage IV according to the FIGO 2009 staging system (FIGO stage IV) pelvic endometriosis-associated malignancy with direct invasion of the rectal wall by the USL adenocarcinoma. The patient underwent six cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with paclitaxel and carboplatin given every three weeks. Over five years after finishing treatment, there are no signs of recurrence. This paper describes an unusual case where deep infiltrating endometriosis of the uterosacral ligament led to malignant transformation. During long-term treatment and surgery for endometriosis, the potential for malignant transformation and the malignant characteristics of endometriosis should be fully considered. Prompt and thorough surgical intervention is crucial.

papers.abstract: Ultrasound-based risk models provide a valuable tool to support non-expert clinicians in evaluating adnexal masses, potentially reducing unnecessary surgeries for benign conditions. However, their implementation in clinical practice across China remains suboptimal, and direct comparisons of their diagnostic accuracy within this specific population are still needed. To evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of three ultrasonography-based risk models-the International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) Simple Rules (with expert adjudication for inconclusive cases), the IOTA Assessment of Different Neoplasias in the Adnexa (ADNEX) model, and the Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS)-for distinguishing benign from malignant adnexal lesions in a Chinese cohort. This retrospective diagnostic study was conducted at a single Chinese academic medical center and included consecutive patients aged 18 to 89 years with adnexal masses that were managed surgically between January 2023 and December 2024. Each adnexal lesion was systematically evaluated using the IOTA Simple Rules, ADNEX model, and O-RADS classification. The diagnostic performance of these models was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and likelihood ratios, using surgical pathology as the reference standard. A secondary analysis evaluated the models' performance stratified by menopausal status. An additional analysis was to evaluate the supplementary value of tumor markers for the O-RADS model. A total of 459 female patients with a 15.5% malignant tumor prevalence were included. Mean age was 43.0 (15.2) years overall, with 40.7 (14.4) in benign and 55.3 (13.3) in malignant cases. Overall, 121 (26.4%) patients were postmenopausal. The AUCs for discriminative performance of the ADNEX and O-RADS models were 0.95 (95%CI, 0.93-0.97) and 0.96 (95%CI, 0.94-0.97), respectively. After converting the ADNEX continuous individualized risk into the discrete ordinal categories of O-RADS, the ADNEX performance was reduced to an AUC of 0.92 (95%CI, 0.90-0.95). The AUC of the Simple Rules was 0.95 (95%CI, 0.93-0.97) and yielded a sensitivity of 95.8% (95%CI, 88.1%-99.1%), specificity of 94.3% (95%CI, 91.5%-96.4%). For a binary comparison of all models (benign vs malignant), a uniform 10% risk threshold (O-RADS score of 4-5) was used. The sensitivity and NPV of all models were above 91% and 98%, respectively. The O-RADS model exhibited the highest sensitivity (97.2%; 95%CI, 90.2%-99.7%), whereas the Simple Rules model demonstrated superior specificity 94.3% (95%CI, 91.5%-96.4%) and the highest PPV (75.6%; 95%CI, 65.4%-84.0%). The sensitivities were higher for menopausal groups, while the specificities were higher for premenopausal patients for the ADNEX and O-RADS model. The addition of tumor markers did not improve the diagnostic sensitivity or specificity of the O-RADS model. In this diagnostic study of a Chinese cohort, the Simple Rules, ADNEX, and O-RADS models demonstrated effective performance in distinguishing benign from malignant adnexal lesions, consistent with previous reports from European and American populations. The use of such risk-stratification models can enhance the accuracy and reproducibility of adnexal mass assessment, particularly for non-specialist clinicians, and may support clinical decision-making and potentially reduce​ avoidable surgical interventions.

papers.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has demonstrated substantial clinical efficacy across HER2-expressing malignancies. However, interstitial lung disease (ILD) represents a clinically relevant and potentially serious adverse event associated with its use, requiring early recognition, exclusion of alternative etiologies and coordinated multidisciplinary management. Delayed identification may increase the risk of severe pulmonary toxicity and premature discontinuation of an otherwise highly effective therapy. In this manuscript, we aim to provide practical guidance on the early detection and management of T-DXd-related ILD. A structured multidisciplinary discussion involving oncologists, pneumologists, and radiologists was conducted to evaluate the epidemiology, risk factors, diagnostic pathways, and management strategies for ILD in patients treated with T-DXd. Evidence from the published literature was reviewed to inform and support the panel's recommendations. ILD may arise in up to 15% of patients receiving T-DXd. While most events occur during the first year of treatment, continued vigilance is warranted throughout therapy. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) is essential for early detection, and prompt treatment interruption combined with timely corticosteroid therapy is critical to prevent progression. The panel emphasized the importance of standardized imaging protocols, structured radiologic reporting, early multidisciplinary involvement, and patient education to facilitate prompt recognition and management. Proactive surveillance strategies, including baseline and interval HRCT, multidisciplinary collaboration and patient-centered monitoring, are essential to minimize ILD-related morbidity while preserving access to T-DXd therapy. The implementation of standardized clinical pathways and the development of biomarker-driven approaches may further improve personalized ILD risk management.

papers.abstract: Patients undergoing treatment for cutaneous melanoma are generally considered cured after a period of 5 years, since most recurrences manifest within three to 5 years. However, some patients can present with a delayed recurrence of melanoma beyond a 10-year timeframe. To identify clinicopathologic factors associated with survival in patients with cutaneous melanoma who developed metastatic recurrence at least 5 years after primary diagnosis. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of 30 patients with cutaneous melanoma developing metastatic recurrence at least 5 years post-diagnosis. The cohort contained 18 women and 12 men (mean age 50.2; range 25-76). Variables included age, sex, BRAF status, site, melanoma subtype, Breslow thickness, ulceration, Clark level, regression, and recurrence localization. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and post-recurrence survival (PRS) were evaluated via Cox proportional hazards models. Mean OS, PFS, and PRS were 168.7, 130.4, and 43.7 months, respectively. Eight patients (27%) died. Tumors averaged 2.61 mm Breslow thickness; 50.0% were BRAF-mutant, 53.3% ulcerated, and 50.0% truncal. Recurrences were locoregional (cutaneous, subcutaneous, in-transit, nodal) in eight (26.7%) and distant in 21 (70.0%); one lacked data. Female sex predicted better univariate OS (HR 0.055, 95% CI 0.01-0.47; p = 0.008) and multivariate PFS (HR 0.364, 95% CI 0.14-0.93; p = 0.035). Increasing age predicted shorter multivariate PFS (HR 1.072, 95% CI 1.03-1.12; p = 0.001). Histologic regression (HR 3.557, 95% CI 1.04-12.17; p = 0.043) and BRAF status (HR 0.413, 95% CI 0.18-0.94; p = 0.034) independently impacted PFS. Kaplan-Meier showed longer OS and PFS in women, and longer PFS in patients younger than 50 years. Delayed recurrence can manifest over a decade post-diagnosis. Female sex and younger age correlate with favorable survival. These findings underscore the necessity of continued clinical vigilance and patient counseling beyond 10 years, although larger cohorts are needed to validate late-recurrence risk stratification.

papers.abstract: Pulmonary carcinoids (PCs) are rare, well-differentiated, neuroendocrine lung tumors with limited treatment options for advanced disease, underscoring the need for targeted therapies. PCs typically exhibit a low mutational burden. Although MEN1 and chromatin-modifier mutations are known contributors, potentially actionable alterations remain poorly characterized. To better define therapeutic opportunities, we evaluated oncogenic fusions and variants across 17 cancer-associated genes in a large retrospective PC cohort. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded primary tumors from Helsinki University Hospital (n = 119, collected between 1990 and 2020) were subjected to targeted RNA-based fusion and variant analysis using the Archer FusionPlex Lung v2 assay. The most frequent recurrent genetic rearrangements involved ALK (n = 5), BRAF (n = 3), FGFR2 (n = 3), and NTRK3 (n = 2), each featuring diverse fusion partners. Variant analysis identified BRAF, EGFR, FGFR1, and FGFR3 as the most frequently mutated genes, although only 2.2% (n = 4) of all detected variants were classified as oncogenic. Notably, 66.7% of all oncogenic or likely oncogenic variants occurred in BRAF and EGFR. Oncogenic variants were identified in ALK, BRAF, EGFR, and ERBB2. Although all FGFR1-3 variants were of uncertain significance, their frequency (34.1% of all detected variants), together with the three FGFR2 fusions, suggested that FGFR alterations may be biologically relevant in PCs. Despite the typically muted genomic landscape of PCs, our study revealed a small yet therapeutically relevant subset of alterations. The findings further characterized the molecular profile of PCs and identified potentially actionable molecular subgroups. While these alterations were not associated with disease-specific survival or metastatic status, they support consideration of molecular profiling in selected patients with advanced disease.

papers.abstract: The partial volume effect influences the results of volumetrics performed on MRI sequences with different slice thicknesses. Although a standardized brain tumor imaging protocol with high-quality 1 mm slices is recommended, segmentation is still commonly performed on thicker slices, especially in retrospective studies. We aimed to quantify the impact of different slice thicknesses on volumetric measurements of brain tumors, using treatment-naive glioblastoma as a representative example. Volumes were measured on T1-weighted contrast-enhanced (CE) sequences using semiautomatic segmentation across three predefined slice thicknesses: 1 mm ("thin"; reference measurement), 3 mm ("intermediate"), and 5 mm ("thick"). Data from 46 patients with the availability of all three slice thicknesses were statistically analyzed, including repeated-measures ANOVA with post hoc comparisons, Bland-Altman analysis, correlations, and linear regression. The tumor volumes measured increased with slice thickness, with mean values of 36.4 cm3 ("thin"), 38.6 cm3 ("intermediate"), and 41.0 cm3 ("thick"). Repeated measures ANOVA showed significant differences between groups (p < 0.01). The mean deviation of the tumor volumes on "thick" relative to "thin" slices was 16% (±10%). Bland-Altman analysis and linear regression confirmed systematically higher measured volumes on "thick" slices. Tumor size on "thin" slices correlated negatively with the percentage deviation on "thick" slices (r = -0.56; p < 0.01). Volumetric measurements obtained from "thick" slices showed systematically higher tumor volumes and greater variability relative to the 1 mm reference. Volumetric data obtained from different slice thicknesses should not be combined, or concepts for adjustment should be considered to maintain methodological consistency and reliability in volumetric studies. We advocate the use of high-quality 3D 1 mm imaging for volumetric analysis whenever possible.

papers.abstract: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and PSA density (PSAD) are widely used for prostate cancer (PCa) screening, but their diagnostic thresholds have not been differentially adjusted for ethnic groups in clinical practice. This multicenter study aimed to establish the distribution of PSA and PSAD in Chinese men without PCa and compare these values with published data from African American (AA) and Caucasian American (CA) men to assess potential racial disparities. We analyzed 528 biopsy-negative Chinese men from two tertiary centers, comparing their age-adjusted PSA/PSAD with published AA/CA data. Additionally, we compared PSA/PSAD distributions and the proportion of men exceeding the conventional PSA cutoff (4 ng/mL) across racial groups. PSA levels showed a weak but significant positive correlation with age (r = 0.121, p = 0.005), whereas PSAD did not (r = -0.032, p = 0.465). Notably, Chinese men without PCa exhibited significantly higher mean PSA and PSAD than AA and CA men (PSA: 17.28 vs. 7.97 vs. 4.30 ng/mL, p < 0.001; PSAD: 0.28 vs. 0.19 vs. 0.11 ng/mL/mL, p < 0.001). Using a PSA cutoff of 4 ng/mL, the specificity for PCa detection was substantially lower in Chinese men than in AA and CA men at matched sensitivity levels. This study reveals striking racial differences in baseline PSA and PSAD among men without PCa, with Chinese men demonstrating markedly higher values than AA and CA counterparts. These findings challenge the universal application of current PSA thresholds and underscore the need for race-specific adjustments to optimize PCa screening accuracy.

papers.abstract: Alterations in the composition of the gut microbiota have been associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), with growing evidence indicating that specific microbes can have an impact on the tumour microenvironment. In this study, we investigated the associations of an oral pathobiont consortium comprising P. stomatis, F. nucleatum sensu lato and P. micra with the tumour immune microenvironment and the clinical presentation of CRC patients. Bacterial levels were quantified in fresh frozen tumour tissues using qPCR and the tumour immune environment was analysed using multiplex immunohistochemistry and multispectral imaging, profiling cytotoxic T cells, T-helper 1 cells, regulatory T cells, B cells, macrophages and regulatory immune checkpoint molecules (CTLA-4, PD-1 and PD-L1). Tumours with polymicrobial intratumoural co-occurrence were more frequently right-sided and exhibited microsatellite instability compared with tumours containing low bacterial levels or high levels of F. nucleatum sensu lato alone. Furthermore, polymicrobial tumours exhibited an altered tumour immune microenvironment, with decreased infiltration of FOXP3+ T regulatory cells and CD68+ macrophages, and increased tumour cell expression of PD-L1 in the tumour centre. Polymicrobial tumours were also associated with poorer patient survival. In conclusion, our findings suggest a link between the co-occurrence of P. stomatis, F. nucleatum sensu lato and P. micra and an altered tumour immune microenvironment in CRC. Elucidating the relationship between bacterial species and immune marker expression may enable the development of improved prognostic and predictive biomarkers, as well as new possibilities for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression (CIM) is the most common adverse reaction of tumor chemotherapy and may lead to treatment delay, dose reduction, life-threatening infection, and poor prognosis. Current predictive methods remain suboptimal, with insufficient interpretability and limited clinical application. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for early CIM risk prediction using routine laboratory data. A total of 1,000 cancer patients from Northeast Yunnan Central Hospital between January 2024 and January 2025 were enrolled and divided into a case group (n=500, with myelosuppression) and a control group (n=500, without myelosuppression).All observed samples were randomly split into a training set (70%) and a validation set (30%). The Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) was used to select optimal variables for model construction. The predictive performance of 15 different ML models was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1-score, Youden's index, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), decision curve analysis (DCA), and residual boxplots. The best-performing model was selected for SHAP-based interpretability analysis and internally validated using a confusion matrix, clinical impact curve, and calibration curve.Additionally, 488 patients treated at Northeast Yunnan Provincial Central Hospital between June 2025 and November 2025 were selected as an independent external validation cohort for external validation. After screening, 15 clinical indicators were used for ML model development. All models demonstrated excellent discrimination. The LightGBM model showed the best overall performance (AUC: 0.999 [0.998-1.000]; sensitivity: 0.986; specificity: 0.989; accuracy: 0.987; PPV: 0.989; NPV: 0.986; F1-score: 0.987; Youden's index: 0.974). According to the LightGBM model, CIM risk increased when the following feature thresholds were met: white blood cell count 10%, red blood cell count <4×1012/L, mean platelet volume <8 fL, and plateletcrit <0.1%.In the independent external validation (n=488), the LightGBM model remained stable and reliable, with an AUC of 0.940 (95% CI: 0.920-0.959), sensitivity of 0.818, specificity of 0.888, accuracy of 85.2%, and favorable calibration and clinical net benefit. The LightGBM prediction model developed in this study can enable early identification of high-risk patients, providing a reference for healthcare providers to implement early interventions.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal predictive model by integrating radiomic features from B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (DCE-US) parametric imaging, as well as clinical and conventional ultrasound features, for preoperative prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) complicated with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). A total of 191 patients with pathologically confirmed HT-complicated PTC were retrospectively enrolled between December 2023 and July 2025. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=133) and a validation set (n=58) at a 7:3 ratio using a random number generator. Radiomic features were extracted from BMUS images and DCE-US peak enhancement parametric maps. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and interclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process including the Mann-Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors of CLNM were identified using multivariate logistic regression incorporating clinical and ultrasound features. Three predictive models were constructed: a clinical-ultrasound model, a radiomics model, and a combined multi-modal model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis. TG-Ab, TR-Ab, extrathyroidal extension, filling defects, BMUS Rad-score, and DCE-US Rad-score were independent predictors of CLNM (P < 0.05). In the training and validation sets, the combined model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.936 and 0.916, respectively, which were significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (AUC = 0.825, 0.876) and the clinical-ultrasound model (AUC = 0.760, 0.800; DeLong test, P < 0.05). Calibration curves showed good model fitting. DCA confirmed that the combined model provided greater clinical net benefit. NRI and IDI verified that the combined model significantly improved CLNM prediction performance. SHAP analysis revealed that DCE-US Rad-score was the most important predictor for CLNM. A multi-modal predictive model combining dual-modality ultrasound radiomic scores (BMUS and DCE-US) with clinical and ultrasound features can effectively and robustly predict CLNM in patients with HT-complicated PTC and performs better than single-modal models. This model provides an objective reference for the formulation of individualized surgical strategies.

papers.abstract: Approximately 35% of patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) progress to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), highlighting the limitations of PSA as a stand-alone monitoring biomarker. This study aimed to construct a peripheral blood mRNA-based prognostic model for progression to mCRPC, evaluate the prognostic value of the identified biomarkers, and explore the biological role of the top-performing gene in prostate cancer cells. Single-cell transcriptomic data (GSE288878) were analyzed to screen for mCRPC-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs). A prospective cohort study was conducted on newly diagnosed mHSPC patients who received first-line androgen deprivation therapy (ADT)-based treatment, from whom peripheral blood samples were collected for transcriptome sequencing. The intersection of DEGs from GSE288878 and our cohort defined the gene signature. Following random splitting of the dataset into development and validation sets (7:3), we used an Elastic Net-regularized Cox model to derive a prognostic model for mCRPC-free survival. TCGA prostate cancer samples were used to analyze the association between biomarker genes and progression-free survival (PFS). In vitro experiments investigated the biological role of the gene with prognostic significance in blood and cancer tissues. Five candidate genes (SLC25A39, GRB10, SELENBP1, SLC6A8, and YBX3) were identified as closely associated with mCRPC. We constructed a prognostic model, with an AUC for predicting 1-year mCRPC-free survival of 0.89 (0.80-0.97) in the development set and 0.83 (0.62-1.00) in the validation set. We identified elevated SLC6A8 expression in peripheral blood as an independent risk factor for progression to mCRPC. In the TCGA database, elevated SLC6A8 expression in prostate cancer tissue was identified as an independent risk factor for shorter PFS. Pharmacological inhibition of SLC6A8 significantly suppressed CRPC cell proliferation, decreased glycolytic metabolite levels, and downregulated glycolysis-associated gene expression. The prognostic model effectively predicted progression to mCRPC in patients with mHSPC receiving first-line therapy. SLC6A8 may serve as a prognostic biomarker and promote prostate cancer progression through enhanced glycolysis.

papers.abstract: The combination of targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and locoregional treatment has established conversion therapy as a viable strategy for China Liver Cancer Staging (CNLC) stage IIb/IIIa hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, upon meeting the criteria for tumor resectability after successful conversion, it remains controversial whether surgical resection (SR) provides superior survival benefits compared to continued medical treatment (CMT), and the optimal timing for surgery is still undefined. We retrospectively analyzed 363 CNLC stage IIb/IIIa HCC patients who met strict tumor resectability criteria after a conversion regimen of lenvatinib, anti-PD-1 antibodies, and transarterial chemoembolization (TACE). Patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 255) and an internal validation cohort (n = 108) at a 7:3 ratio. Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized to balance the baseline characteristics. Survival outcomes were compared and prognostic nomograms were developed using Cox proportional hazards regression. After 1:3 PSM, the training cohort comprised 63 SR patients and 189 CMT patients. The SR group demonstrated significantly better median overall survival (mOS, 32.1 vs. 24.3 months; P 90 days from meeting resectability criteria to surgery, and a pre-operative AFP to baseline AFP (at the time resectability was met) ratio > 1, were significantly associated with worse OS. For CNLC stage IIb/IIIa HCC patients achieving tumor resectability following conversion therapy, SR is significantly associated with improved survival outcomes compared to CMT. Based on our exploratory findings, surgery within 90 days of meeting resectability criteria may be considered a beneficial strategy, provided that the pre-operative AFP level does not exceed the level observed when resectability was initially achieved.

papers.abstract: Metastatic dissemination and therapeutic failure, the major determinants of breast cancer mortality, are fundamentally driven by epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and its phenotypic plasticity. This review comprehensively interrogates the regulatory logic of EMT plasticity in breast cancer, decoding the intricate interplay among transcription factor cascades, epigenetic landscapes, non-coding RNA circuits, and microenvironmental cues that collectively sustain tumor cell adaptability. We further delineate the translational frontier, summarizing recent advances in pharmacologically targeting EMT core regulators and discussing the promise and pitfalls of plasticity-modulating therapeutic paradigms. Ultimately, by integrating evolving knowledge from basic and translational research, we present a cohesive framework aimed at bridging mechanistic understanding with clinical decision-making, with the goal of refining precision therapy for breast cancer patients.

papers.abstract: The malignant progression of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is closely associated with the acquisition of ferroptosis resistance by tumor cells; however, the upstream regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aims to elucidate the function and molecular mechanisms of the methyltransferase-like 7B (METTL7B)/pleckstrin homology domain-containing family A member 4 (PLEKHA4)/aurora kinase A (AURKA) signaling axis in ferroptosis resistance in PTC. Our results showed that PLEKHA4 was highly expressed in PTC. By binding to kelch-like protein 12 (KLHL12), PLEKHA4 inhibited KLHL12-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of AURKA, thereby stabilizing the AURKA protein and enhancing ferroptosis resistance in PTC cells. Upstream, METTL7B stabilized PLEKHA4 mRNA and upregulated its expression through N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed that knockdown of METTL7B increased ferroptosis sensitivity and suppressed PTC progression. This study reveals a novel paradigm in which PLEKHA4, as an effector of m6A modification, regulates ferroptosis by interfering with ubiquitin-mediated degradation, providing a theoretical basis for targeting this pathway in the treatment of PTC.

papers.abstract: Cancer-related psychological distress remains underaddressed globally. Virtual interventions offer promising alternatives but lack evidence for enhancing Psychological Capital (PsyCap) in chemotherapy patients. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a virtual social interaction intervention on PsyCap in patients undergoing chemotherapy. This single-blind randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 76 chemotherapy patients hospitalized in the oncology ward of Imam Sajjad Hospital, Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran. Participants were selected via convenience sampling and then allocated to intervention or control groups using an odd-even (alternating) assignment method. The intervention group participated in 6 weeks of virtual social interactions, consisting of asynchronous materials (recorded audio, short videos, images, PDF, and PowerPoint files) uploaded weekly to Iranian messaging platforms (Eitaa), as well as live synchronous group sessions conducted on the Skyroom platform with a minimum of 10 participants per session. The control group received standard care. The PsyCap was measured using Luthans' Psychological Capital Questionnaire at both baseline and post-intervention. The Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) models (A/B) were adjusted for baseline scores and age. The intervention group showed improvements across all outcomes, with the total PsyCap score increasing by 23.6 points. Components significantly increased: self-efficacy by 5.8 points, resilience by 5.8, hope by 5.5, and optimism by 6.5 (p 1). Virtual social interactions significantly enhance PsyCap in chemotherapy patients. However, to confidently generalize these findings and make recommendations, similar studies need to be conducted and replicated in larger, multicenter trials.

papers.abstract: Component C1q binding protein (C1QBP) is known as an important regulator of mitochondrial plasticity and is involved in antitumor immune response in cancers. Nevertheless, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) still remains largely unknown. C1QBP expression in LUAD and adjacent normal samples was compared by Wilcoxon test, and the corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to estimate its diagnostic value. Associations between C1QBP expression levels and different clinical traits were analyzed by chi-square test; K-M curves were applied for analyzing survival differences, and univariate and multivariate Cox analysis were employed to construct the C1QBP-related nomogram model. Furthermore, GSEA and immune analysis were performed to explore the mechanism. Finally, rhC1QBP was applied to cultured mast cells in vivo to investigate its regulatory effect on mast cell dysfunction, and sh-C1QBP was injected into LUAD xenograft mice to explore the effect of C1QBP knockdown on tumor growth in vivo. The C1QBP expression level, with a preferable diagnosis effect, was significantly different between LUAD and normal samples, and was notably interrelated with gender, TNM stage, and Fustat in LUAD patients. LUAD patients with high C1QBP levels displayed lower survival rates. Our nomogram based on C1QBP expression and T stage displayed decent prediction capability. There was a significant difference in C1QBP expression in plasma cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), activated CD4 memory T cells, resting mast cells, and eosinophils between LUAD patients and the controls. Upregulation of C1QBP with rhC1QBP treatment promoted mast cell ferroptosis through interacting with the Cullin3 protein. While Fer-1, a ferroptosis inhibitor, counteracted rhC1QBP induced ferroptosis in mast cells. Knockdown of C1QBP inhibited tumor growth in xenograft mice. C1QBP may be a promising potential prognostic biomarker in LUAD and a potential therapeutic target by affecting the immune microenvironment of LUAD patients.

papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have emerged as potential treatment options for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) resistance. We evaluated their efficacy and safety in this setting. PubMed, Embase,and the Cochrane Library were searched for prospective clinical studies. Overlapping reports were assessed before endpoint-specific synthesis. Comparable proportional outcomes from non-randomized studies were pooled using random-effects models, whereas randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were summarized separately. Eight eligible clinical study reports were included. Four non-randomized reports contributed five independent underlying trial datasets; however, the ORR and DCR meta-analysis each included four non-overlapping analytical estimates because one pooled Dato-DXd estimate represented two underlying trial datasets that were not entered separately. The pooled ORR was 39.2%(95% CI,31.1%-48.0%),and the pooled DCR was 78.9%(95% CI,72.3%-84.2%).Three comparable non-overlapping datasets contributed to the grade ≥3 TEAE analysis, yielding a pooled incidence of 65.2%(95% CI,50.2%-77.7%),whereas four analytical datasets contributed to the ILD analysis, with a pooled reported incidence of 6.0%(95% CI,4.1%-8.5%).Two RCTs provided comparative evidence supporting sac-TMT, particularly for ORR and PFS. ADCs showed antitumor activity after EGFR-TKI resistance, but efficacy and toxicity varied across platforms. Additional randomized trials and biomarker-informed studies are needed to define the optimal use of individual ADCs. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261288638, identifier CRD420261288638.

papers.abstract: The optimal timing and fractionation of perioperative stereotactic radiotherapy for resected brain metastases remain uncertain. We evaluated the comparative evidence for preoperative and postoperative stereotactic treatment and the validity of indirect comparisons. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov for comparative studies published or posted through 12 August 2026. Primary outcomes were local control or failure, leptomeningeal disease (LMD), and radiation necrosis (RN). Compatibility for quantitative synthesis was assessed by treatment definition, analysis unit, outcome definition, effect measure, and estimation method. Compatible patient-level hazard ratios (HRs) for local failure were combined in an exploratory fixed-effect network model. Incompatible evidence and patient-level and lesion-level estimates were synthesized separately. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were also assessed. Sixteen comparative studies were included, comprising six randomized trials and ten non-randomized studies. Three studies provided compatible patient-level HRs and formed a four-treatment local-failure network. Postoperative single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) reduced local failure compared with observation in one randomized trial (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.24-0.88). Estimates for preoperative versus postoperative single-fraction SRS (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 0.38-6.49) and postoperative single-fraction SRS versus three- to five-fraction treatment (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.09-7.32) were imprecise. All indirect comparisons had wide confidence intervals that included 1. Each direct comparison was informed by one study, and the network contained no closed loop. Some indirect estimates were sensitive to the evidence selected for the single-fraction versus fractionated-treatment comparison. Evidence for LMD and RN did not form compatible connected networks and was synthesized descriptively. Certainty was moderate for postoperative single-fraction SRS versus observation and very low for the remaining local-failure comparisons. Randomized evidence supports postoperative single-fraction SRS over observation for reducing local failure. However, current evidence does not establish a reliable hierarchy among preoperative SRS, postoperative single-fraction SRS, and postoperative fractionated treatment. Evidence for LMD and RN remains insufficient for network comparison. Treatment decisions should account for individual clinical characteristics until adequately powered prospective comparisons become available. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261341468.

papers.abstract: Current global data on epidemiology, treatment patterns, outcomes, and care pathways for patients with gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) are needed. A systematic review included publications from Embase and Medline (interventional: 2005-2025; observational: 2021-2025) and conference abstracts (2022-2024). Benign gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) studies, case reports, and case series were excluded. Treatment response rates and 95% CIs were calculated from aggregated data. Of 117 included studies, 66.7% (n=78) were cohort studies; 54.7% (n=64) were conducted in Asia. GTN incidence from GTD varied from 6.2% in the UK to 16.8% across Asian studies. Methotrexate and dactinomycin were the most common real-world first-line treatments in low-risk GTN. Second-line and high-risk patients' treatment included diverse multiagent regimens and immunotherapy. Across trials, first-line treatment response with dactinomycin (82.9%) was higher than methotrexate (70.5%); in observational studies, response was similar and inversely associated with GTN risk score. Nausea and other gastrointestinal events were more common with dactinomycin than methotrexate. Incidence of GTN varied by region and setting. Consensus supports methotrexate or dactinomycin as first-line therapy in low-risk GTN. Treatment options were more diverse in high-risk GTN and later-line regimens. Unmet needs to improve response rates and minimize toxicity persist.

papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a lethal hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis.COVID-19 co-infection further complicates clinical management and worsens survival outcomes of AML patients, highlighting the need to explore the molecular interplay between the two diseases. In this study, we initially screened 109 common differentially expressed genes shared by AML and COVID-19 from public transcriptomic datasets, which were closely involved in tumor progression and viral pathogenesis. We further characterized their biological functions, constructed protein interaction and TF-miRNA regulatory networks, and established an AML prognostic model to evaluate the tumor immune microenvironment. Combining survival analysis, clinical correlation, immune infiltration assessment and m6A modification analysis, SLC15A3 was preliminarily screened as a candidate prognostic gene for AML. Subsequent weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning (ML) and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses further identified SLC15A3 as a promising prognostic biomarker for AML. Finally, RT-qPCR and Western blotting assays verified its aberrant expression in AML cells. Consistent with bioinformatic prediction,SLC15A3 serves as a shared candidate biomarker for AML and COVID-19,although its mechanistic role linking AML and SARS-CoV-2-related inflammation requires further functional validation.

papers.abstract: Tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) is a life-threatening oncologic emergency well-characterized in hematologic malignancies but considered rare in solid tumors. In breast cancer, TLS has been documented only in sporadic case reports, and the evolving treatment landscape-including CDK4/6 inhibitors, PI3K inhibitors, novel endocrine agents, and antibody-drug conjugates-may introduce previously unrecognized TLS risks. The only prior review on this topic was published in 2021 and has been superseded by numerous new cases. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from January 2000 to June 2026 for case reports and case series describing TLS in patients with breast cancer, following PRISMA guidelines. TLS diagnosis was verified against Cairo-Bishop criteria. Data on patient demographics, tumor characteristics, precipitating factors, laboratory abnormalities, management, and outcomes were extracted and analyzed descriptively. Twenty cases of TLS from 20 publications were identified, with one additional case of successful TLS prevention. All patients had stage IIB-IV disease, with the majority (90%, 18/20) having stage IV disease; liver metastases were present in 55% (11/20). Precipitating factors included endocrine therapy (n=4, 75% mortality), HER2-targeted therapy (n=4, 50% mortality), chemotherapy (n=6, 50% mortality), radiotherapy (n=2, 50% mortality), PI3K inhibitor (n=1, survived), immunotherapy-chemotherapy combination (n=1, survived), and spontaneous TLS (n=2, 50% mortality). Overall TLS-related mortality was 50% (10/20). Endocrine therapy-associated TLS-predominantly aromatase inhibitors-carried the highest mortality (75%, 3/4). The only surviving patient in this group achieved long-term remission following supportive management. TLS in breast cancer, though rare, carries a high mortality rate approaching 50%. Notably, endocrine therapy-particularly aromatase inhibitors-emerges as a previously underappreciated TLS trigger with disproportionately poor outcomes. With the expanding use of novel targeted and endocrine agents in advanced breast cancer, clinicians should maintain heightened vigilance for TLS, especially in patients with high tumor burden and hepatic metastases. Early recognition and prompt intervention are essential to improve outcomes. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261429658.

papers.abstract: Gastroesophageal junction cancer is a rising global health concern with variable outcomes. The availability to high-volume cancer centers may influence survival, yet disparities related to geography and socioeconomic status remain poorly defined. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the SEER 21 Research Plus database (2000-2022). A total of 40,273 patients with locoregional gastroesophageal junction cancer were included. Patient-level variables included age, sex, race, histology, stage, and survival. Socioeconomic and geographic variables included county-level median household income and rural-urban residence. State-level volume was defined according to the number of high-volume esophageal cancer centers within each patient's state of residence: high-volume (≥ 2 centers), moderate-volume (1 center), and low-volume (no centers). The primary outcome was overall survival. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations between patient-, socioeconomic-, geographic-, and state-level factors and survival. Residence in states with lower-volume centers was associated with worse outcomes than residence in states with high-volume centers. Each step toward lower-volume categories was associated with an increased hazard of death (HR 0.923, 95% CI 0.899-0.949, p < 0.001). While stage at diagnosis varied significantly across hospital volume categories (p < 0.001), no clear pattern of more advanced stage in lower-volume states was observed. Patients with adenocarcinoma had a 25% lower hazard of death compared to those with squamous cell carcinoma (HR 0.752, 95% CI 0.726-0.780, p < 0.001). Female gender was associated with a statistically significant increase in hazard of death compared to males (HR 1.042, 95% CI 1.013-1.072, p = 0.004). Additionally, higher median household income was associated with improved survival (HR 1.006, p < 0.001 per category increase), and urban residence (HR 1.036, p < 0.001) was independently associated with improved survival. Survival in locoregional gastroesophageal junction cancer is influenced by both tumor biology and healthcare access. Residence in states with high-volume centers, adenocarcinoma histology, higher income, and urban residence were independently associated with improved survival, highlighting disparities tied to regional resource availability within the United States.

papers.abstract: Colon and rectal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) have varying disease behaviors, presentations, and outcomes. Rectal NETs are detected early; colonic NETs present later and more aggressively. We compared demographic, tumor, treatment, and survival characteristics of colonic versus rectal NETs. This retrospective cohort study used SEER data (2000-2022) to identify adults with colonic or rectal NETs. Demographic, tumor, and treatment characteristics were compared by tumor site. Five-year overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier statistics and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Additional site-specific analyses evaluated stage and treatment patterns by race, ethnicity, and household income. Twenty-four percent of 30 246 patients had colonic NETs, and 76.0% had rectal NETs. Rectal NET patients were younger (55.7 vs. 62.9 years, p < 0.001) and more often Black, Asian, or Hispanic. Colonic NETs were more frequently poorly differentiated (43.9% vs. 7.0%), larger (median 30 vs. 5 mm), and more likely to have liver metastases (27.7% vs. 3.7%). Rectal NETs underwent local excision (92.1%), colonic NETs required colectomy (72.3%). Rectal NETs demonstrated higher 5-year OS (88.8% vs. 55.8%) and CSS (93.8% vs. 58.2%, p < 0.001). Stage III colonic NETs had higher CSS than rectal NETs (67.3% vs. 53.5%, p < 0.001). Colonic and rectal NETs have distinct clinicopathologic profiles, treatment patterns, and stage-specific outcomes. These findings support site-specific evaluation while emphasizing the importance of stage and tumor biology in prognosis.

papers.abstract: Core needle biopsy (CNB) is commonly used to diagnose bone tumors, but characteristics of tibial lesions may affect its diagnostic performance. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-guided CNB for tibial lesions, factors associated with diagnostic success, and outcomes of nondiagnostic biopsies. We retrospectively reviewed 272 patients with tibial lesions treated at a quaternary sarcoma referral center from 2016 to 2022, of whom 43 underwent CT-guided CNB. Patient, lesion, and pathologic characteristics were evaluated for associations with diagnostic outcomes. Of 43 biopsies, 58.1% were diagnostic, 79.1% accurate, and 55.8% successful. Accuracy was significantly higher for non-diaphyseal than diaphyseal lesions (27/31 vs. 7/12; p = 0.038). Lesions < 5 cm were less likely to achieve diagnostic success than lesions ≥ 5 cm (OR 0.231, 95% CI 0.064-0.836; p = 0.022). Of 18 nondiagnostic CNBs, 12 underwent subsequent incisional biopsy, identifying five malignancies. CT-guided CNB of tibial lesions has modest diagnostic yield, with lower accuracy in diaphyseal lesions and reduced diagnostic success in lesions < 5 cm. These findings may inform biopsy planning and identify patients more likely to require incisional biopsy for definitive diagnosis.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the incidence, timing and anatomical pattern of relapse after cytoreductive surgery (CRS) for pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP), and identify predictors of overall and early (within 12 months) relapse. Retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing curative-intent CRS for appendiceal PMP at a single institution (2016-2025), recording the site of first relapse. Predictors of progression-free survival (PFS) and early relapse were evaluated using Cox and logistic regression. Among 204 patients, CC-0/1 cytoreduction was achieved in 89% and HIPEC in 92%. At 37.1-month median follow-up, 89 patients (44%) relapsed; 3-year PFS and overall survival were 50.2% and 75.6%. Relapse was predominantly intraperitoneal, most often the pelvis and small bowel/mesentery (25% each). Histology and completeness of cytoreduction independently predicted PFS: low-grade (HR 2.18), high-grade (HR 2.79) and signet-ring PMP (HR 4.35) vs acellular mucin, CC-2/3 (HR 2.18), and male sex (HR 1.74). Early relapse occurred in 34 patients (17%), independently predicted by high-grade histology (OR 5.06) and CC-2/3 (OR 3.55). Relapse after CRS for PMP is predominantly intraperitoneal, most often the small bowel/mesentery and pelvis. Histology and completeness of cytoreduction are the principal determinants of overall and early relapse, supporting risk-stratified surveillance and selective repeat cytoreduction.
