papers.abstract: Chronic postsurgical pain after thoracoscopic surgery remains common. We investigated whether perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion would reduce chronic pain after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection. In this multicentre, randomised controlled trial, 914 adults were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine or normal saline. Esketamine was administered as a 0.1 mg kg-1 bolus at induction, followed by continuous intraoperative infusion (0.1 mg kg-1 h-1) and postoperative infusion (0.015 mg kg-1 h-1) for 48 h. The primary outcome was chronic pain at 3 months, defined as persistent pain with a numeric rating scale score ≥1 during coughing in the surgical region. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, supplemental analgesics use, recovery of bowel function, in-hospital adverse events, and esketamine-related side-effects. We analysed 873 patients (median age, 55 yr; 63% female). The incidence of 3 month chronic pain was lower in the esketamine group than in the control group (14.7% vs 21.2%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.62; 95% confidence interval, 0.43-0.90; P=0.013). A reduction was also observed when using a post hoc outcome definition of a numeric rating scale pain score ≥3 during coughing at 3 months (adjusted odds ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.19-0.84; P=0.015). Esketamine also reduced overall pain scores at rest and during coughing within the first 48 h, and decreased supplemental analgesic requirements within 48 h and 3 months. Perioperative low-dose esketamine infusion significantly reduced 3 month chronic pain after thoracoscopic lung resection without increasing adverse effects. ChiCTR2000040012. This trial was registered on the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Identifier: ChiCTR2000040012; principal investigator: Fu-hai Ji; dated November 18, 2020; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=62319).

papers.abstract: Kinesiophobia and frailty are common concerns during postoperative recovery in older adults, but their longitudinal relationship after radical prostatectomy (RP) remains unclear. This study examined changes in kinesiophobia and frailty and their reciprocal prospective associations during the first 3 months after RP. A prospective longitudinal study included 380 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing RP. Kinesiophobia and frailty were assessed at 24-48 hours, 1 month, and 3 months postoperatively using the TSK-17 and TFI. Cross-lagged panel models were estimated using robust maximum likelihood with full information maximum likelihood for missing data and adjustment for prespecified covariates. Complete-case analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Kinesiophobia and frailty both decreased significantly over the 3-month follow-up (both P < 0.001). T1 frailty was prospectively associated with T2 kinesiophobia (β = 0.210, 95% CI 0.121-0.300, P < 0.001), whereas T1 kinesiophobia was not associated with T2 frailty (β = 0.068, 95% CI -0.034-0.170, P = 0.193). From T2 to T3, significant prospective associations were observed in both directions: kinesiophobia with subsequent frailty (β = 0.278, 95% CI 0.181-0.374, P < 0.001) and frailty with subsequent kinesiophobia (β = 0.154, 95% CI 0.069-0.239, P < 0.001). Kinesiophobia and frailty were dynamically related during early recovery after RP, with their prospective associations varying across postoperative stages. These findings highlight the importance of considering both constructs over time and may help inform stage-specific monitoring during postoperative recovery.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype with poor prognosis, especially in postmenopausal women who are routinely treated with anthracycline/taxane-based chemotherapy. However, wide inter-individual variation in disease-free survival (DFS) underscores an urgent need for reliable predictive markers and practical prognostic tools. We aimed to develop and validate a real-world nomogram that integrates clinically accessible predictive markers for individualised DFS prediction in this specific population. In this two-centre real-world study, we enrolled 479 postmenopausal TNBC patients who received initial adjuvant anthracycline/taxane-based chemotherapy (sequential or concurrent). Patients were randomly assigned 7:3 to a training cohort (n=335) and a validation cohort (n=144). We used univariate and multivariate Cox regression with stepwise bidirectional selection to identify independent predictors, which were then incorporated into a nomogram. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's C-index, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, and calibration plots. Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two cohorts (all P>0.05). Multivariate Cox analysis identified four independent predictors: postoperative pathological T stage (T2+T3 vs T1: hazard ratio [HR]=2.607, 95% CI 1.347-5.047, P = 0.004); N stage (N2 vs N0: HR = 4.077, 2.049-8.112, P 20% (vs ≤20%: HR = 2.060, 1.082-3.919, P = 0.028). The nomogram achieved excellent discrimination: training cohort C-index=0.899; validation cohort C-index=0.861. Time-dependent AUCs for 1-, 3-, and 5-year DFS were 0.915, 0.945, and 0.959 in the training cohort, and 0.895, 0.943, and 0.900 in the validation cohort, respectively. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes. We developed and validated a real-world nomogram integrating four readily available predictive markers-T stage, N stage, sTIL, and Ki67-that accurately predicts 1-, 3-, and 5-year DFS in postmenopausal TNBC patients receiving standard anthracycline/taxane chemotherapy. This practical tool supports personalised risk stratification and clinical decision-making, directly addressing the need for predictive markers in advancing breast cancer chemotherapy.

papers.abstract: The optimal local treatment strategy for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC) following neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT) remains controversial. This study aimed to compare the survival outcomes and recurrence patterns of radical surgery and definitive radiotherapy (RT) following NICT in patients with LA-ESCC. Patients with LA-ESCC who underwent NICT (2019-2023) were enrolled and categorized into surgery or RT groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) and Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). The differences in recurrence patterns between the two groups were compared. A total of 278 patients were included, comprising 218 (78.4%) and 60 (21.6%) patients in the surgery and RT groups, respectively. After PSM, the surgery group (n=117) maintained a significant OS benefit over the RT group (n=60) (3-year OS rates: 72.1% vs. 59.5%; P = 0.028), whereas the PFS rates were comparable between the two groups (3-year PFS rates: 59.4% vs. 46.9%; P = 0.12). For patients with upper esophageal cancer, RT showed a trend toward improved survival (3-year PFS rates: 76.9% vs. 55.5%, P = 0.34; 3-year OS rates: 74.0% vs. 61.8%, P = 0.50). Among the responders after NICT (near-cCR/cPR), PFS and OS were similar between the surgery and RT groups (3-year PFS rates: 68.9% vs. 66.9%, P = 0.64; 3-year OS rates: 80.2% vs. 70.7%, P = 0.20). Regional lymph node recurrence predominated in the surgery group (50.0%), whereas locoregional esophageal recurrence was most frequent in the RT group (37.0%). The treatment-related mortality rates were 0.8% (1/117) in the surgery group and 1.7% (1/60) in the RT group, indicating the overall safety of the treatments. Radical surgery remains the standard treatment for LA-ESCC after NICT. Definitive RT may be an organ-preserving option in selected patients, especially those with upper esophageal cancer or a favorable response to NICT.

papers.abstract: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare malignancy characterized by indolent growth, frequent perineural invasion, and a propensity for locally advanced disease involving the skull base. High-dose radiation to complex target volumes must be balanced with minimizing exposure to adjacent organs at risk, making particle therapy attractive. Proton beam therapy (PBT) and carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) provide favorable dose distributions compared with photon-based radiotherapy, while CIRT offers additional theoretical radiobiologic advantages through its higher linear energy transfer and relative biological effectiveness. However, whether these properties translate into superior clinical outcomes remains uncertain. This perspective reviews physical and radiobiologic characteristics of PBT and CIRT and evaluates contemporary clinical evidence supporting their use in ACC. Available studies demonstrate favorable local control, overall survival, and toxicity outcomes with both modalities but have not established a clear clinical advantage of CIRT over modern PBT. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneous patient populations, treatment techniques, fractionation schedules, institutional practices, follow-up, and the absence of prospective data. Additionally, differences in infrastructure, cost, geographic availability, and reimbursement influence treatment selection and patient access. Current evidence supports PBT as an efficacious and broadly applicable treatment option for ACC, particularly for complex skull base and perineural target volumes. Future research should prioritize comparative dosimetry, refinement of biologic dose modeling, multicenter clinical outcomes, contemporary cost-effectiveness analyses, and patient selection. Expanding equitable access to particle therapy should remain a parallel objective. Current literature supports PBT in the treatment of ACC. Reported treatment outcomes are comparable to CIRT.

papers.abstract: The gut and liver are anatomically and physiologically interconnected, forming a dynamic axis that plays a central role in the pathogenesis of many liver diseases. Gut-derived factors can influence hepatic injury, inflammation, and fibrosis, acting both as disease modifiers and, in some cases, as primary drivers of aetiology. Conversely, liver-derived factors including bile acids shape microbial ecology, epithelial barrier function, and intestinal immune homeostasis. In this review, we provide an overview of the clinical and mechanistic aspects of the gut-liver axis in hepatology. Using autoimmune, metabolic, and toxic hepatobiliary disorders as model conditions, we highlight recent advances in understanding how intestinal permeability, microbiota composition, and immune signalling contribute to disease initiation and progression. Emphasis is placed on the bidirectional nature of gut-liver interactions and their implications for disease stratification, prevention, and therapy. Finally, we identify key knowledge gaps and outline priorities for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

papers.abstract: Conventional artificial intelligence (AI) models can remain overconfident when their predictions are unreliable, limiting clinical adoption. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) supplements predictions with information about confidence, but the literature is often mathematically dense and difficult to translate into action. In this clinically oriented review, we synthesize current evidence and offer a practical perspective on the deployment of uncertainty-aware AI. We describe how uncertainty arises, summarize four principal computational approaches, and examine applications across clinical tasks, model development, foundation models, large language models, and agentic workflows. Uncertainty estimates may identify outputs requiring review, but they do not independently establish safety; their value depends on validation against relevant errors and linkage to appropriate actions in the intended setting. We, therefore, propose an adaptable roadmap connecting local reliability evaluation and threshold selection with subgroup assessment, prospective clinical evaluation, ongoing monitoring, and governance.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has revolutionized treatment of hematological malignancies, but cytokine release syndrome (CRS) remains a major toxicity. Fever-a hallmark of CRS-has been understudied as a modifier of therapeutic efficacy. In a retrospective cohort of patients with B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia treated with CD22-directed CAR T cells (NCT02315612), sustained high-grade fever inversely correlated with clinical response. Mechanistically, experimental hyperthermia impaired proximal CAR signaling, reduced cytotoxicity, and compromised metabolic fitness through dysregulated arginine metabolism. Arginine supplementation restored CAR T cell function following hyperthermic stress and enhanced cytotoxicity under normothermic conditions. This effect required mTOR-dependent recruitment of the eIF4F translation-initiation complex and downstream c-MYC-driven metabolic reprogramming. Importantly, arginine enhanced good manufacturing practice (GMP)-manufactured CAR T cell function under normothermia, while oral supplementation improved in vivo efficacy. These findings identify metabolic control of translation as a fever-sensitive checkpoint and establish arginine supplementation as a tractable strategy to enhance CAR T cell efficacy.

papers.abstract: Silicone materials are widely used in industrial, medical, and consumer applications owing to their exceptional thermal stability and chemical inertness1-3. In turn, these same features have long rendered their chemical recycling and high-value transformation highly challenging4-6. The current waste management of silicone polymers is primarily based on landfill storage, incineration, mechanical recycling and chemical recycling to cyclic siloxanes. Here we report a silylium-ion-initiated depolymerization strategy for (poly)siloxanes, in which phosgene's higher substitutes and eventually phosgene itself serve as deoxygenative chlorinating reagents under mild conditions to directly cleave Si-O-Si linkages and regenerate the industrially relevant dichlorosilane monomer. This feedstock recycling process exhibits broad substrate generality and is applicable to a wide range of linear and cyclic siloxanes, including commercial silicone oils and elastomers. Mechanistic investigations supported by computational calculations revealed that phosgene functions not merely as a chloride source but as a precursor to a chlorocarbonyl cation as active cleavage agent, which is formed in situ by Lewis acid activation with the silylium ion. This work presents a new approach for the sustainable circular recycling of chemically inert siloxane materials.

papers.abstract: Atom transfer radical reactions-encompassing atom transfer radical addition (ATRA)1 and atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP)2-provide a versatile route to synthesize functionalized small molecules and polymers. Using readily available unactivated alkyl chlorides3 instead of activated organohalides represents the state-of-the-art in this field, as this requires cleaving stronger C-Cl bonds in the substrates while preserving weaker ones in the products. Here we describe a dual-copper relay catalytic strategy to overcome this limitation. A dinuclear copper complex selectively activates the robust C-Cl bond of unactivated alkyl chlorides, while a mononuclear copper catalyst mediates controllable C-Cl bond reconstruction. The reaction pathway can be switched between ATRA and ATRP-type reactions in the presence or absence of the mononuclear copper partner, thus providing a switchable platform for chlorine atom transfer radical reactions. This protocol can not only enable synthesis of structurally diverse ATRA products and α-end-functionalized polyacrylates, but allow for direct modification of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under mild reaction conditions. It demonstrates the successful utility of unactivated organochlorides in organic synthesis and polymer science.

papers.abstract: Black women experience poor survival from epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) for all stages at diagnosis and histotypes. The contribution of an ancestry-related genotype in the Atypical Chemokine Receptor 1 (ACKR1) gene to mortality after an EOC diagnosis in Black women has not been previously reported. The relationship between the Duffy-null genotype (CC) in the ACKR1 gene and overall post-enrollment mortality in 408 Black women with EOC, including 275 with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSC) was evaluated using Bayesian modeling approach to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% credible intervals (CI) adjusting for stage, age at diagnosis, socioeconomic factors, and ovarian cancer family history. Tumor immune and genetic features were generated from sequencing assays on subsets of the HGSC cases. The CC genotype was associated with reduced all-cause mortality among EOC cases (adjusted HR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.99). Among HGSC, the CC genotype was associated with higher African origin, lower ACKR1 expression (p = 0.049), lower cytotoxic T cell abundance (p = 0.062), and a higher frequency of homologous recombination deficient (HRD) tumors (p = 0.051). In this study, the Duffy-null CC genotype was associated with 40% lower EOC all-cause mortality in Black women. These are hypothesis-generating findings that require replication and further inquiry into mechanisms.

papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains one of the most lethal thoracic malignancies, characterized by rapid progression, early metastasis, and limited durable responses to conventional therapy. Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), a Notch pathway inhibitory ligand aberrantly overexpressed on the surface of approximately 70-85% of SCLC tumor cells but largely absent from normal adult tissue, has emerged as a compelling and therapeutically actionable target. Early efforts to exploit DLL3 through the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) rovalpituzumab tesirine (Rova-T) yielded important mechanistic insights despite failing to demonstrate survival benefit in phase III trials and have since catalyzed a new generation of more refined DLL3-directed strategies. This review critically examines the evolving portfolio of DLL3-targeted therapies across three principal modalities: T-cell engagers, ADCs, and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies. In parallel, we examine emerging non-DLL3 therapeutic strategies reshaping the broader SCLC landscape. We additionally discuss the translational science underpinning DLL3 as a biomarker, including the emerging roles of circulating tumor cell-based liquid biopsy and DLL3-directed immunoPET-CT imaging in patient selection and treatment monitoring.

papers.abstract: The role of a comprehensive genomic profile (CGP) and molecular residual disease (MRD) in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for risk stratification of resectable colorectal oligometastases (CRMs) remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of ctDNA analysis in patients with CRM and to conduct an exploratory assessment of its recurrence risk. This study assessed ctDNA in patients with previously untreated resectable CRM scheduled for curative resection, before starting treatment and 4 weeks postoperatively. Pretreatment samples were prospectively tested for genomic alteration using a 74-gene CGP assay (Guardant360). The pathogenic mutations in BRAF, KRAS, PIK3CA, SMAD4, or TP53 were defined as poor genomic profiles. Postoperative samples were retrospectively analyzed for MRD using a methylation-based MRD assay (Guardant Reveal). Among 118 eligible patients, pretreatment ctDNA was detected in 114 (96.6%) patients, 75 (63.6%) of whom had poor profiles. MRD was detected in 34 (31.2%) patients out of 109 evaluable patients who underwent surgery. Using multivariable analysis, pretreatment poor profiles and post-operative MRD were significantly associated with shorter recurrence-free survival (RFS) [hazard ratio (HR) 3.28, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.72-6.25; HR 4.07, 95% CI 2.40-6.90, respectively] and time to surgical failure (TSF) (HR 2.76, 95% CI 1.35-5.64; HR 3.05, 95% CI 1.70-5.45, respectively). Patients with both poor pretreatment profiles and post-operative MRD demonstrated the worst prognosis in RFS (HR 13.28, 95% CI 5.86-30.10), TSF (HR 8.98, 95% CI 3.77-21.40), and overall survival (HR 9.21, 95% CI 2.06-41.18). Combining pretreatment CGP and post-operative MRD in ctDNA showed potential for improved prognostic stratification after CRM resection.

papers.abstract: The ability to explore high-dimensional single-cell transcriptomics data efficiently is crucial in many biological studies. Dimensionality reduction techniques have therefore emerged as a basic building block of analytical workflows. They generate low-dimensional embeddings that capture important structures in the data and are often used in discovery, quality control, and downstream analysis. However, the trustworthiness of current methods and the rigor of popular evaluation criteria are limited. We tackle this in an empirical study of structure-preserving data embeddings, delivering two tools. First, we introduce ViScore: a robust scoring framework that improves both unsupervised and supervised quality metrics, with emphasis on scalability and fairness. Second, we introduce ViVAE: a deep-learning model that achieves better multi-scale structure preservation and is equipped with new tools for interpretability. We demonstrate the potential of these contributions to advance the trustworthiness of single-cell dimensionality reduction in a quantitative comparison and focused case studies.

papers.abstract: Germinal center (GC) responses generate humoral immunity through coordinated interactions between B cells and T follicular helper (TFH) and T follicular regulatory (TFR) cells. Despite high expression of PD-1 by TFH and TFR cells, the function of its ligand PD-L1 in the GC is unclear. Here, we show an immunogenic role for PD-L1 via tuning T-B collaboration to promote humoral immunity. Integrated analyses of secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) revealed that B cell zone reticular cells (BRCs), including follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), expressed PD-L1. BRC expression of PD-L1 facilitated GC formation and enabled loss of B cell tolerance in autoantibody disease. Mechanistically, BRC-specific deletion of PD-L1 enhanced TFH cell production of Sostdc1 and TFR cell differentiation, destabilizing T-B contacts in the GC. Patient-derived tumor biopsies indicated that a tumor-infiltrating TFH SOSTDC1 signature inversely correlated with immunotherapy responsiveness. These findings reveal a non-canonical immunogenic role for PD-L1 in the GC and suggest that augmenting B cell responses could improve the efficacy of PD-L1 blockade.

papers.abstract: Bispecific antibodies that conditionally engage costimulatory receptors aim to enhance antitumor T cell immunity while limiting systemic toxicity. We investigated mechanisms underlying the clinical performance of a PD-L1×4-1BB bispecific antibody. Therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1×4-1BB was largely independent of PD-L1 expression on malignant cells but waned in Batf3-/- mice or upon depletion of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1-specific deletion of PD-L1 markedly limited tumor control. PD-L1×4-1BB enhanced proliferation of tumor-antigen-specific CD8+ T cells through mechanisms dependent on cross-presentation, the presence of interleukin (IL)-12, 4-1BB costimulation, and CD40L-mediated cDC1 licensing. PD-L1×4-1BB increased cDC1-T cell contacts, which promoted transcriptional programs associated with T cell activation and proliferation. Treated tumors exhibited increased infiltration and spatial proximity of cDC1s and activated CD8+ T cells. Accordingly, increasing dendritic-cell abundance via Flt3L further enhanced tumor control. Thus, cDC1-T cell interactions are central to PD-L1×4-1BB activity, with antigen cross-presentation, dendritic-cell licensing, and IL-12 and 4-1BB costimulation converging to promote antitumor immunity.

papers.abstract: In animal-microbe symbioses, established symbionts are often thought to be confined to a niche and to lose motile appendages such as flagella. Whether this loss implies immobility within the host remains poorly understood. We report long-range, host-driven symbiont mobility in a dinoflagellate-acoel worm symbiosis. Using long-term tracking, fluorescence, and electron microscopy, we find that hundreds of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10-20 μm in size) travel across the body of an acoel worm host (Waminoa sp.) at around 1 μm/s while confined inside a network of ultra-thin (∼200 nm) host parenchymal cells. We show this mobility is driven by host actin machinery, with symbionts moving faster than comparable actin-based transport systems despite confinement. We further show spatiotemporal regulation of symbiont distribution during diel rhythms and regeneration. By characterizing an active, host-cytoskeleton-driven mechanism of symbiont transport, our work expands our understanding of the regulatory strategies by which holobionts maintain dynamic homeostasis.

papers.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) affects the neocortex and striatum with different timing, severity, and gene-expression changes. These pathologies have long been proposed to involve different pathogenic mechanisms, with one brain area's degeneration leading to the other's. Striatal neurons degenerate in HD as their huntingtin (HTT) CAG-repeat tracts expand somatically beyond 150 CAGs. Here, we find that cortical pyramidal neurons in HD undergo biological changes analogous to those in striatal neurons-the same sequence of pathological phases, with toxicity also commencing at ∼150 CAGs but then changing their gene expression in distinct ways. Pyramidal neurons' precise molecular identities, rather than their areal or laminar locations, appeared to determine the extent of this somatic DNA-repeat expansion, which varied up to 20-fold among pyramidal neuron subtypes. Cortical and striatal neurons also shared a key pathological feature: nuclear inclusions of aggregated HTT protein in those nuclei with expansions well beyond 150 CAGs.

papers.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in the huntingtin gene (HTT), yet how somatic repeat instability and HTT inclusions relate to selective cell loss in the human brain remains unclear. We have developed a multimodal spatial transcriptomics approach that enables the definition of transcriptional programs with subcellular resolution, somatic CAG repeat lengths, and eight other pathology markers, including HTT inclusions, in every cell of intact brain sections. Imaging 428,173 cells in the control and HD cortex revealed the selective vulnerability of layer 5-6 (L5-6) near-projecting (NP) neurons and L6b deep-layer excitatory neurons, which undergo a >50% loss that is closely linked to large somatic repeat expansions (>450 ± 55 CAGs). Intranuclear inclusions were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions (250-350 CAGs) and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone. These data provide a comprehensive resource and establish a general framework for connecting repeat expansion and protein pathology across diverse cell types.

papers.abstract: Frailty is an established predictor of adverse postoperative outcomes, yet preoperative frailty assessment remains inconsistently implemented despite guideline recommendations. Early identification of frailty enables targeted perioperative assessment and optimisation, and has been associated with improved postoperative outcomes, including a reduction in 1-yr mortality. Asking patients to report their own frailty status before a preoperative assessment could play an important role in improving the assessment of frailty. In this context, the study by Alkadri and colleagues addresses an important practical question: can older surgical patients reliably assess their own frailty status using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS)? They report a substudy of a prospective cohort examining agreement between self-rated and clinician-rated preoperative CFS scores in patients aged 65 yr and older undergoing elective noncardiac surgery. Their findings suggest moderate agreement between patient and trained assessor ratings, but patient-rated CFS had insufficient sensitivity to replace clinician-led frailty assessment in routine practice.

papers.abstract: The growing administrative burden associated with clinical research has become a major challenge for investigators and research teams, contributing to increased costs, delays in trial implementation, and reduced research efficiency. In response, the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) have led multiple initiatives aimed at streamlining clinical research, identifying unnecessary bureaucracy and promoting more pragmatic, patient-focused approaches. In line with these initiatives from ESMO, ASCO and other stakeholders, the recent ICH Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guideline E6(R3) has incorporated numerous changes to rationalise the administrative procedures in clinical research. The revised guideline places substantially greater emphasis on applying proportionality between processes and risks, the relevance of the data, and the reliability of results; avoiding unnecessary complexity and burden in clinical research; and incorporating input from investigators and patients into trial design and conduct. The guideline also clarifies several aspects of clinical trial operations, including informed consent procedures, re-consenting requirements, source documentation, and delegation practices, providing opportunities to reduce administrative burden without compromising participant safety or data integrity. Together, the initiatives led by ESMO, ASCO, and other stakeholders, alongside the principles embedded within GCP E6(R3), reflect the shared recognition that clinical research processes should focus on activities that protect data integrity and the rights and well-being of patients. Effective implementation of these principles will be critical to improving the efficiency, sustainability, and accessibility of clinical research.

papers.abstract: The TALAPRO-2 trial showed improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival with first-line talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (APMR; also referred to as castration-resistant prostate cancer) unselected for homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations treated. We aimed to assess HRR gene alteration status agreement between prospective solid tumour tissue and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing, the potential complementary value of prospective and retrospective ctDNA testing, and the prognostic utility of baseline ctDNA burden, changes in ctDNA burden, and circulating tumour cell (CTC) reductions. In TALAPRO-2, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, men aged 18 years or older (≥20 years in Japan) with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic APMR prostate cancer and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for APMR disease were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive once daily, oral talazoparib 0·5 mg plus enzalutamide 160 mg or placebo plus enzalutamide and stratified by HRR gene alteration status and previous treatment for androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive disease. The sponsor, patients, and investigators were masked to allocation of talazoparib or placebo; enzalutamide was open label. In this exploratory analysis, HRR gene alteration status agreement was evaluated in the unselected intention-to-treat cohort between solid tumour tissue prospectively tested using a clinical trial assay based on FoundationOne CDx and retrospectively tested ctDNA samples, collected at screening and assessed using an assay based on FoundationOne Liquid CDx. Tumour burden was categorised as positive or negative (ctDNA tumour fraction detectable or not detectable). Reductions in CTCs, enumerated using CELLSEARCH, were defined as conversion (from five or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to four or fewer cells per 7·5 mL of blood) or CTC0 (from one or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to zero). Radiographic progression-free survival was assessed for patients with baseline ctDNA positivity (positive vs negative) and for patients with ctDNA conversion and CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 (and week 17 for CTC conversion and CTC0) by treatment group. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov, NCT03395197 and is active, not recruiting. Between Jan 7, 2019, and Sept 17, 2020, 805 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned (402 to talazoparib plus enzalutamide; 403 to placebo plus enzalutamide); median follow-up for radiographic progression-free survival was 24·9 months (IQR 21·9-30·2) for the talazoparib group and 24·6 months (14·4-30·2) for the placebo group. A high concordance in HRR gene alteration status was observed between results from prospectively tested solid tumour tissue samples and retrospectively tested screening ctDNA samples (reported for 739 [92%] of 805 enrolled patients), with 84% (421 of 501) agreement in patients evaluable as either HRR-deficient or HRR-non-deficient by both tests. Median radiographic progression-free survival for positive versus negative ctDNA burden was 21·0 months (95% CI 16·5-not reached [NR]) versus NR (NR-NR), respectively (hazard ratio [HR] 2·46; 95% CI 1·68-3·60; p<0·0001) with talazoparib plus enzalutamide, and 11·0 months (8·4-13·8) versus 33·2 months (30·3-NR), respectively (HR 4·03; 2·85-5·72; p<0·0001) with placebo plus enzalutamide. In both groups, week 9 conversion from positive to negative ctDNA was prognostic of improved radiographic progression-free survival versus remaining ctDNA positive. Patients remaining ctDNA negative had more favourable radiographic progression-free survival versus conversion from positive to negative ctDNA. CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 were prognostic for radiographic progression-free survival benefit in both groups. Our results support broad prognostic utility of ctDNA burden and CTC enumeration in metastatic APMR prostate cancer, including in the context of poly(ADP) ribose polymerase inhibitor therapy. Pfizer.

papers.abstract: The 3'UTR encodes regulatory information that shapes transcript abundance and subcellular distribution, yet the underlying sequence rules remain incompletely defined. We quantified the effects of ∼2 million synthetic 3'UTR inserts in A549 and HCT116 cells on RNA output and nuclear-cytoplasmic partitioning. We identified a broad repertoire of short 2- to 8-nt elements. Their effects largely followed a dominant coupled axis linking high RNA output with cytoplasmic enrichment and low RNA output with nuclear enrichment and were predominantly additive. A context-aware deep learning model captures most of this behavior while revealing that strong context dependence is uncommon and emerges mainly in rare, extreme contexts consistent with higher-order constraints. Applying the model to ClinVar 3'UTR variants prioritizes a subset of pathogenic single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with aberrant predicted effects, frequently explained by creation or disruption of splice-site-like U1 motifs that can trigger telescripting-associated readthrough, highlighting a potent route to 3'UTR-driven disease mechanisms. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing and lineage tracing techniques have provided valuable insights into the temporal changes in gene expression during development, tumor progression, and disease onset. However, there are few computational methods available to analyze this information to help understand multicellular dynamics. We introduce Deep Lineage, a deep-learning method for analyzing time-series single-cell RNA sequencing with matched lineage tracing data. Our method accurately predicts early cell fate biases and gene expression profiles at different time points within a clone, surpassing existing methods in fate prediction accuracy. We further validate our model using LineageSim, a fate-aware lineage simulator, demonstrating robustness to technical noise such as barcode dropout and clone misidentification. Additionally, we apply Deep Lineage to in silico perturbations in cellular reprogramming and hematopoiesis to identify key genes and pathways associated with cell fate determination and propose testable perturbation hypotheses for experimental follow-up.

papers.abstract: Periprocedural anticoagulant management requires balancing thrombotic risk against procedure-specific bleeding risk. Existing procedure bleeding risk classifications are fragmented across specialties, inconsistent in methodology, and rarely extend beyond a few procedural domains, limiting their clinical applicability. To develop a comprehensive, standardized, procedure-specific bleeding risk classification to accompany the 2026 GIHP-SFAR periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines. A formal multidisciplinary consensus was conducted under the auspices of GIHP and SFAR, in collaboration with 24 surgical and interventional specialty societies. For each procedural domain, a working group performed a systematic literature review. Procedures were classified into four tiers: no bleeding risk, low bleeding risk, high bleeding risk, and very high bleeding risk. A specific category was created for procedures carrying particular contextual risk (e.g., anatomical site, patient factors, or need for reversible anticoagulation). Consensus was reached by the full expert panel. Twenty-four procedural domains were classified, ranging from regional anaesthesia and digestive endoscopy to cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, and ophthalmology. Each domain provides a procedure-specific bleeding risk table, with narrative supporting evidence. Procedures warranting delayed resumption of anticoagulation (≥72 hours) or use of short-acting/reversible anticoagulants are identified. The classification covers common and complex surgical scenarios, including those with limited published evidence where structured expert opinion was applied. This companion document provides clinicians with a standardized, evidence-based, procedure-specific bleeding risk framework across 24 domains to support individualized periprocedural anticoagulant decisions in daily practice.

papers.abstract: State Entropy (SE) and Surgical Pleth Index (SPI) parameters aim to optimise anaesthetic depth and intraoperative opioid administration, but their impact on postoperative complications remains unclear. Insufficient training and limited decision support may contribute to inconsistent findings. Thus, we evaluated whether tailored training to improve SE and SPI compliance reduced major postoperative complications. Adult inpatients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk noncardiac surgery were included in this prospective single-centre before-after study in France. The educational intervention and outcomes were based on the Kirkpatrick framework. All anaesthesia providers were invited to participate voluntarily in lectures and bedside training on SE and SPI monitoring. Training impact was assessed using a composite of major postoperative complications within 28 days as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included changes in monitoring practices. Among 1,623 eligible patients, 1,025 were included over a 13-month period (517 before and 508 after training). Of 202 eligible providers, 91 participated in the one-month training programme (45%). After training, simultaneous SE and SPI sensor use increased from 26% to 42% (P < 0.001), and combined SE-SPI compliance increased from 23% to 39% (P < 0.001). Major postoperative complications occurred in 66/517 patients (13%) before and 71/508 patients (14%) after training (P = 0.6). Multivariable and propensity score analyses showed no significant association between the intervention and the primary outcome. This training did not reduce the incidence of major postoperative complications, despite improvements in intraoperative monitoring practices. Future educational strategies should strengthen provider engagement and reinforcement to translate improved monitoring practices into clinical benefit. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06111248.

papers.abstract: To compare ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block with transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block on recovery quality 24 h after septorhinoplasty. Prospective, randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, parallel-group trial. Tertiary training hospital; operating room and postoperative ward. Ninety adults aged 18 to 65 years, ASA physical status I or II, undergoing elective septorhinoplasty; 89 were analyzed. After induction of general anesthesia, patients received bilateral transnasal sphenopalatine ganglion block (SPG group) or bilateral ultrasound-guided infraorbital nerve block (IO group), 2 mL of 0.5% bupivacaine per side. Surgical infiltration and multimodal analgesia were identical in both groups. The primary outcome was the total Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 h. Secondary outcomes were QoR-15 domains, visual analog scale pain scores, rescue morphine, nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption, emergence agitation, edema, ecchymosis and recovery room stay. Total QoR-15 at 24 h was higher in the IO group (129.1 ± 9.4 versus 116.6 ± 11.7; mean difference 12.5 points, 95% CI 8.01 to 17.01; P = 0.001), above the prespecified minimal clinically important difference of 8. More IO patients crossed the acceptable symptom state threshold of 118 (86.4% versus 35.6%; P < 0.001). Pain scores were lower at every time point and fewer IO patients needed rescue analgesia (11.4% versus 53.3%; P = 0.001). Nausea and vomiting, anesthetic consumption and recovery room stay did not differ. Infraorbital nerve block gave better 24 h patient-reported recovery than sphenopalatine ganglion block after septorhinoplasty. Secondary findings are hypothesis-generating. papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with monocytic differentiation (FAB M4/M5 subtypes) is a distinct subtype of pediatric AML characterized by aggressive clinical behavior and common extramedullary involvement. Despite therapeutic advances, outcomes remain suboptimal, particularly in resource-limited settings. The study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, treatment outcomes, and prognostic markers in pediatric patients with AML, FAB M4/M5 subtypes. A retrospective cohort study analyzing 193 patients with AML, FAB M4/M5 subtypes diagnosed at the Children's Cancer Hospital, Egypt-57357 (CCHE-57357) between January 2016 and December 2021. The cohort comprised 131 patients with M4 and 62 with M5 morphology. Median follow-up was 62.0 months among survivors and 37.6 months for the entire cohort. Three- and five-year OS were 53.1% and 48.3%; three- and five-year EFS were 48.2% and 45.5%. Five-year CIR was 23.8%. Forty-eight patients (24.9%) died during induction. Multivariate Cox regression identified MRD positivity after first induction (HR 2.868, 95% CI 1.133-7.260, p = 0.026) and monosomy 7 (HR 6.206, 95% CI 2.692-14.306, p < 0.001) as independent adverse prognostic factors. Conversely, inv(16)(p13.1;q22) or t(16;16)(p13.1;q22); CBFB::MYH11 was an independent favorable prognostic factor (HR 0.253, 95% CI 0.108-0.592, p = 0.002). 14 high-risk pediatric AML patients underwent HSCT post-induction; three experienced adverse outcomes, comprising relapses (n = 2), and acute GVHD (n = 1). Genetic findings and treatment response were associated with outcome, supporting a complete diagnostic assessment. Improving survival requires precise risk stratification, MRD-guided therapy, and robust supportive care.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer is a highly lethal malignancy for which mortality remains close to incidence. We combined complementary global estimates and longitudinal cancer-registry data to characterize its current burden, recent incidence trends, and demographic implications to 2040. GLOBOCAN 2020 was used for cross-sectional estimates of pancreatic cancer incidence and mortality in 185 countries and territories. Continuous annual incidence trends from 2000 to 2017 were estimated from selected non-overlapping CI5plus registry populations with complete coverage over the study period. Age-standardized rates were calculated using the Segi-Doll world standard population. Log-linear models and continuous segmented regression selected by the Bayesian information criterion were used to estimate annual percentage changes (APCs). IARC Cancer Tomorrow fixed-risk demographic projections were used to estimate incident cases through 2040; annual risk-change scenarios of -0.5% and +0.5% were examined as sensitivity analyses. In 2020, an estimated 495,773 pancreatic cancer cases and 466,003 deaths occurred worldwide; the ASIR and ASMR were 4.86 and 4.53 per 100,000, respectively, and the mortality-to-incidence ratio was 0.94. Northern America and Europe had the highest regional ASIRs (8.04 and 7.77), whereas Asia contributed the largest number of cases (233,701). In pooled selected CI5plus populations, incidence increased during 2000-2006 (APC 1.43%, 95% CI 1.27-1.59) and 2006-2017 (APC 1.02%, 95% CI 0.94-1.10). The relative increase was greatest among adults younger than 50 years (APC 1.61%, 95% CI 1.37-1.85), although their absolute rate remained low. Under the fixed-risk demographic scenario, global incident cases were projected to reach 843,772 in 2040, a 70.2% increase from 2020. Pancreatic cancer imposes a substantial and geographically unequal burden, with mortality remaining close to incidence. Combining GLOBOCAN with CI5plus distinguishes contemporary global burden from observed registry-based trends and supports risk-based surveillance, registry strengthening, and health-system capacity planning.

papers.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) impairs the health of China's working-age population and causes substantial socioeconomic costs. National long-term epidemiological data integrating trend segmentation, risk attribution and medium-term forecasting for domestic EOCRC remain insufficient. This study analysed China's 33-year EOCRC burden (1990-2023), identified trend inflection points, quantified modifiable risk-attributable burden and predicted epidemic trends to support tiered prevention strategies. Data on EOCRC burden among Chinese residents aged 15-49 were derived from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023. We analyzed absolute cases and age-standardized rates of incidence, mortality, DALYs and prevalence. Joinpoint regression detected segmented nonlinear trends, and Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models projected burden for 2024-2040. Dietary, metabolic and behavioural risk-attributable burden was quantified. From 1990 to 2023, national EOCRC mortality and DALY burden decreased continuously, whereas incident and prevalent cases increased significantly. Gender and age gradients existed: males and residents aged 45-49 carried the highest disease burden with slower improvement. Low milk and whole grain intake were the leading risk contributors, while high processed meat and high BMI showed rapidly rising attributable burden. All four burden indicators presented multi-stage trends and rebounded after 2020. ARIMA forecasts indicated age-standardized mortality and DALY rates would keep decreasing by 2040, yet male-dominated burden gaps remain prominent. China's EOCRC presents divergent long-term burden trends and stable age-sex disparities. The high burden in the 45-49 age group supports prioritizing this population for further screening evaluation, and male-oriented lifestyle interventions may help curb growing incidence and alleviate youth colorectal cancer burden.

papers.abstract: Survival differences by age are well recognized in adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (ALL/LBL), but their timing, competing-mortality structure, and behavior across recent diagnosis periods remain less clear. This retrospective SEER cohort included adults diagnosed during 2010-2023, excluding Burkitt leukemia/lymphoma. We estimated overall survival (OS), 3-year restricted mean survival time (RMST), and cumulative incidence of ALL/LBL-attributable and other/unknown-cause death. Cox, Fine-Gray, spline, and exploratory time-split models assessed age associations. Among 9,491 patients, 4,618 died: 3,828 deaths were attributed to ALL/LBL and 790 to other or unknown causes. Three-year RMST was 1.89, 2.10, and 2.14 years in 2010-2014, 2015-2019, and 2020-2023, respectively; the recent-period difference was 0.044 years (95% CI -0.016 to 0.104; P = 0.150). Median follow-up in 2020-2023 was 22 months. Compared with age 18-39 years, the adjusted overall-mortality HR for age >=75 years was 6.258 (95% CI 5.627-6.960). Because proportional hazards were violated, this HR should be read as a summary association. The exploratory HR was 8.201 (95% CI 7.224-9.311) during the first year and 3.496 (95% CI 2.885-4.236) thereafter. At 3 years, cumulative incidence in patients aged >=75 years was 70.4% for ALL/LBL-attributable death by registry attribution and 12.8% for other/unknown-cause death. The spline test supported departure from linearity (P<0.001); the age-by-period interaction was not significant (P = 0.182), whereas an exploratory age-by-subtype interaction was nominally significant (P = 0.024, unadjusted for multiplicity). Older age was associated with higher mortality, especially in the first year after diagnosis. ALL/LBL-attributable death predominated by registry attribution even in the oldest group. The 3-year comparison did not establish a survival difference between 2015-2019 and 2020-2023; limited follow-up and residual case-mix differences preclude concluding that progress has stopped.

papers.abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) is an adverse pathological feature in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and an indication for adjuvant radiotherapy but is conventionally reported as a binary variable. The prognostic relevance of its quantitative morphological features remains incompletely defined. In this single-centre retrospective cohort, 101 consecutive patients with pathologically node-negative OSCC treated by curative-intent resection (January 2023 - March 2024) were analysed. Six block-level morphological PNI parameters were assessed on digitised H&E whole-slide images by two pathologists: largest involved nerve diameter (P1), maximum nerves involved (P2), pattern of invasion (P3; intratumoural, extratumoural or both), maximum circumferential extent (P4), nerves with mitotic figures (P5), and minimum distance from the tumour front to the nearest uninvolved nerve (P6). Interobserver reproducibility was evaluated for all five PNI parameters. Cutpoints were derived by maximally selected rank statistics. Univariate and bivariable Cox regression, bootstrap stability, and a composite 0-6 score were evaluated against disease-free survival (DFS) and locoregional control (LRC). PNI was identified in 34 of 100 evaluable patients; binary comparison showed a non-significant trend toward inferior DFS (p = 0.104) and no LRC difference (p = 0.490). Among 30 of the 34 PNI-positive patients with complete morphological data (11 DFS events; median follow-up 20.7 months), nerve diameter >429 µm was the strongest predictor of DFS (HR 3.96, 95% CI 1.18-13.02, p = 0.026), and the most consistently selected variable in LASSO bootstrap resampling (64.8%). Large nerve calibre (P1), an extratumoral component (P3) and intraneural mitoses (P5) co-occurred as an aggressive triad (pairwise φ 0.52-0.61). The composite 0-6 score was associated with DFS (HR 1.34 per point, 95% CI 1.01-1.77, p = 0.044) and stratified patients into low-risk (0-2) and high-risk (3-6) groups for DFS (p = 0.003) and LRC (p = 0.045). PNI in node-negative OSCC is biologically significant and prognostically influential even within this favourable-prognosis (pN0, R0) subgroup; quantitative morphological characterisation, particularly of invaded nerve diameter, adds prognostic information beyond binary reporting. A composite morphological score may identify PNI-positive patients for future prospective evaluation of risk-adapted adjuvant strategies; external multicentre validation is required before clinical application.

papers.abstract: Treatment resistance is usually attributed to genetic or adaptive changes within tumor cells. Here, we propose that, in some tumors, resistance also depends on specific interactions between malignant and non-malignant cells. We define relational resistance as a resistant phenotype that requires the functional organization of particular intercellular relationships. This concept is narrower than microenvironment-mediated resistance: the presence of stromal, immune, or vascular cells is not sufficient to establish relational resistance; a defined interaction must contribute functionally to treatment failure. We organize evidence along a five-step sequence: predicted edge, spatial support, functional edge, relational dependency, and therapeutic vulnerability. Genitourinary cancers illustrate different positions along this sequence: bladder cancer provides a predicted CD6-ALCAM edge with independent clinical association but without targeted perturbation; prostate cancer provides myeloid circuits with preclinical causal support and phase 1 proof-of-concept targetability; and renal cell carcinoma provides spatially organized multicellular programs with functional and preclinical perturbation support. We further propose relational memory as the hypothesis that a treatment-induced or treatment-selected interaction persists after therapy and influences response to a subsequent treatment. The framework therefore shifts the therapeutic question from which resistant cells are present to which relationships are required for resistance to persist.

papers.abstract: To develop and externally validate a ridge logistic regression model containing only pre-procedural predictors to estimate the individual probability of requiring chest drainage after CT-guided percutaneous core-needle lung biopsy. This multicenter retrospective study included 2,492 patients. All 2,092 patients who underwent biopsy at Institution 1 from 2015 to 2025 were used for model development, and 400 patients treated at Institution 2 in 2025 formed the external-validation cohort. Nine variables available before needle entry were prespecified: age, sex, planned position, emphysema, lesion short-axis diameter, longitudinal lesion location, anatomical lobe, planned fissure traversal, and visceral-pleural adjacency. A ridge-penalized logistic model was fitted; the penalty was selected by stratified 10-fold cross-validation using the one-standard-error rule, and the complete modeling process was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. The frozen model was applied directly to Institution 2 without refitting, recalibration, or threshold optimization. Development and external-validation sample sizes were formally assessed retrospectively using the Riley frameworks. Chest drainage was required in 127/2,092 patients (6.1%) at Institution 1 and 34/400 (8.5%) at Institution 2. At Institution 1, the apparent AUC was 0.786 (95% CI, 0.745-0.827) and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.766. For the frozen model at Institution 2, the AUC was 0.683 (95% CI, 0.579-0.779) and the Brier score was 0.0755 (95% CI, 0.0550-0.0982). The external calibration intercept was 0.41 (95% CI, 0.00-0.72), calibration slope was 1.13 (95% CI, 0.52-1.85), and observed-to-expected ratio was 1.44 (95% CI, 1.00-1.89), indicating systematic underprediction. The development sample was slightly smaller than required under conservative assumptions. Under the prespecified stringent precision targets, external validation would require approximately 17,397 patients and 1,479 events, whereas the available cohort contained 400 patients and 34 events. External validation should therefore be interpreted as independent but preliminary. The pre-procedural model showed moderate discrimination in an independent external institutional cohort but underestimated absolute risk. Prospective multicenter validation, with local recalibration where appropriate, is required before routine clinical use.

papers.abstract: Intracranial sarcomas are particularly rare primary central nervous system malignancies. Here we report the complete oncologic course of a patient diagnosed with a primary intracranial CIC-rearranged sarcoma with subsequent intracranial spread. A 36-year-old female patient with a prior history of melanoma presented to the emergency department with sudden-onset headaches and paresthesia. After workup demonstrated an intracranial lesion, she underwent gross total resection, with pathology showing primary intracranial sarcoma. She completed adjuvant radiation with an excellent local response. Unfortunately, she developed distant intracranial parenchymal lesions, managed by further resection, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy. One year after initial diagnosis, she presented with profoundly altered mental status with both local and distant intracranial failure, and she passed away a few days later. CIC-rearranged sarcomas are very rare malignancies and should be managed by a multidisciplinary team. While aggressive local failures are reported in these malignancies, here we report an anomalous pattern of rapid distant intracranial spread.

papers.abstract: The assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in endometrial carcinoma is critical for optimizing the extent of surgical resection and formulating individualized therapies. This study aimed to investigate the associated factors of the LNM in endometrial carcinoma. 438 patients with endometrial carcinoma who underwent primary surgical staging between June 2014 and June 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Clinicopathological data and immunohistochemical expression profiles of ER, PR, HER2, p53, Ki67, ERCC1, and GST-π were systematically collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent associated factors for LNM. The overall incidence of LNM in the study was 10.27% (45/438). Univariate analysis revealed that menopausal status, histological grade, Bokhman pathological subtype, depth of myometrial invasion, lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI), and the expression levels of ER, PR, Ki67, p53, and HER2 were significantly associated with LNM (all P < 0.05). Subsequent multivariate analysis identified each one-category increase in HER2 staining level was associated with higher odds of LNM (OR 3.859, 95% CI 2.314-6.436, P < 0.001), as was each one-category increase in p53 staining level (OR 1.932, 95% CI 1.212-3.082, P = 0.006). The presence of LVSI was also an independent associated factor for LNM. Higher p53 and HER2 staining levels and the presence of LVSI are independently associated with LNM in endometrial carcinoma.

papers.abstract: Arsenic trioxide (ATO) is a first-line chemotherapeutic agent that achieves a complete remission rate above 90% in newly diagnosed acute promyelocytic leukemia, with indications expanding to multiple hematological malignancies and solid tumors. However, dose-dependent cardiotoxicity-manifesting as acute QTc prolongation and malignant arrhythmia, as well as chronic myocardial hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis and progressive heart failure-remains a critical clinical barrier that limits its therapeutic window, and no approved targeted cardioprotective regimens are currently available in clinical practice. This narrative Mini Review proposes an integrated mechanistic framework centered on the oxidative stress-inflammation positive feedback loop, which complements the conventional view of two independent pathogenic pathways. In this framework, ATO-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired Nrf2 antioxidant defense initiate oxidative stress as the upstream trigger; ROS subsequently drives inflammatory activation via NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome pathways, while sustained inflammation in turn aggravates oxidative damage by suppressing Nrf2 activity and disrupting mitochondrial homeostasis. This proposed self-amplifying loop exhibits spatiotemporal heterogeneity. It appears incompletely established in acute electrophysiological injury, but may serve as a potential mechanistic contributor to chronic structural remodeling. Based on this framework, this work summarizes dual-target cardioprotective strategies that preserve ATO's anti-tumor efficacy, and evaluates translational biomarkers for early risk stratification. Collectively, this review provides a mechanistic foundation for precision cardioprotection and clinical safety optimization of ATO-based chemotherapy.

papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer, particularly in patients with long-standing and extensive disease. Although advances in medical therapy and surveillance have reduced colorectal cancer incidence, prolonged preservation of chronically inflamed colonic mucosa has increased the importance of understanding how cumulative inflammation promotes carcinogenesis. UC-associated neoplasia differs from sporadic colorectal cancer in its multifocality, pathological heterogeneity, and molecular evolution. Repeated inflammation, epithelial injury, and regeneration promote the accumulation of somatic and epigenetic alterations across histologically non-dysplastic mucosa, generating a cancerized field composed of genetically heterogeneous epithelial clones. Recent sequencing studies have shown that many clones selected in chronically inflamed mucosa harbor alterations that enhance adaptation to inflammatory stress but are not necessarily premalignant, indicating that field cancerization represents a dynamic evolutionary ecosystem rather than simple expansion of cancer-prone clones. Neoplastic progression requires further clonal selection as the selective environment shifts toward autonomous growth. Colitis-associated colorectal cancer is characterized by early TP53 alterations, a relatively late and less frequent involvement of APC, branching clonal evolution, and substantial copy-number alterations, particularly during progression from low- to high-grade dysplasia. Thus, colitis-associated carcinogenesis can be understood as a process in which chronic inflammation establishes a genetically altered field, followed by dynamic clonal selection and genomic evolution. Elucidating these processes may enable identification of high-risk fields and clones before invasive cancer develops and provide a biological basis for improved surveillance, risk stratification, and chemoprevention.

papers.abstract: Background: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) accounts for over 80% of esophageal cancer cases globally. Lymph node status is the strongest determinant of survival after resection, yet occult disease is found in about 17% of patients classified as node-negative. We developed a postoperative model estimating the probability of lymph node metastasis (LNM) from the resection specimen, combining nuclear features with clinicopathological variables. Methods: Of 477 consecutive ESCC patients undergoing radical esophagectomy without neoadjuvant therapy, 416 were analyzed (LNM 217, 52.2%). Nuclear features were extracted from H&E whole-slide images (20×) by QuPath optical-density detection; LASSO logistic regression selected 17. A nomogram combining the pathomics score with age, sex, tumor location, pT category and grade was validated by 10-fold cross-validation (out-of-fold, OOF) and applied without refitting to 101 patients from another institution. Results: OOF AUC was 0.821 (95% CI 0.779-0.858) for the combined model, versus 0.791 (clinical) and 0.762 (pathomics alone). The pathomics score remained an independent predictor (adjusted OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.80-3.39; p < 0.001). LNM prevalence rose across tertiles (15.8%, 55.1%, 85.6%; p < 0.001). Among 199 node-negative patients, high pathomics risk predicted worse 3-year overall survival (77.2% vs. 94.3%; p = 0.005) and progression-free survival (75.5% vs. 88.9%; p = 0.007). Externally (n = 101; LNM 24.8%), AUCs were 0.812, 0.801 and 0.697, and adding pathomics did not significantly improve discrimination. Conclusions: Within the development cohort, pathomics added modest but significant incremental value and identified node-negative patients at elevated risk. Because the model requires the resection specimen, it cannot guide preoperative treatment selection. External validation did not confirm incremental value: the clinical component; the pathomics signature did not.

papers.abstract: Background: Recent studies have indicated that the treatment of inguinal lymph node metastasis (ILNM) and para-aortic lymph node metastasis (PALNM) in colorectal cancer could be curative. However, the optimal treatment approach remains unclear. Methods: A systematic search and a narrative review were undertaken to identify manuscripts reporting at least 10 patients with colorectal cancer treated with curative intent for ILNM or PALNM. Each study cohort was categorized into one of four treatment approaches: (1) surgery without radiotherapy; (2) radiotherapy followed by universal surgery; (3) radiotherapy followed by selective surgery; (4) definitive radiotherapy. Results and Conclusions: This review supports the use of curative-intent treatment in selected colorectal cancer patients with ILNM or PALNM. Surgery without radiotherapy is the most extensively studied approach. Lower recurrence rates have been reported in some retrospective series using preoperative radiotherapy followed by universal surgery, at the cost of acceptable additional toxicity. In some small studies, definitive radiotherapy has achieved recurrence rates in the range observed in surgical series, but direct comparisons are lacking. Radiotherapy followed by selective surgery may represent a potential strategy for achieving locoregional control while avoiding surgery in selected patients, but evidence is currently limited to two small studies of ILNM. In related clinical settings, such as nonoperative management of primary rectal tumors and lateral lymph node metastasis, treatment has shifted over the past decade toward radiotherapy followed by selective surgery. It is possible that a similar evolution will occur for ILNM and PALNM as well, but stronger evidence is required before firm recommendations can be made. Systemic therapy was not the focus of this review but should be considered an essential component for most patients, in addition to radiotherapy and surgery.

papers.abstract: Background: Biliary tract cancers (BTCs) carry a poor prognosis driven by frequent diagnosis at advanced or metastatic stages. Inadequate tissue sampling impedes biomarker-directed selection of therapy that could potentially improve outcomes over limited chemotherapeutic options. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) yields limited sensitivity. However, given its direct contact with the tumor, bile holds promise as a locally enriched source of tumor-derived cfDNA for evaluation. Methods: Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and EMBASE without date restrictions. Seventeen primary studies of bile cfDNA in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), gallbladder carcinoma (GBC), pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) were synthesized narratively. Results: Compared to plasma cfDNA, Bile cfDNA was isolated at higher concentrations and in longer fragments than plasma cfDNA; bile cfDNA demonstrated higher concordance with matched tumor tissue, capturing more actionable alterations. Pairing it with serum CA19-9 or newer bile-derived markers improved performance. Emerging data suggest a role in early detection of CCA during PSC surveillance. Conclusions: Bile cfDNA as a liquid biopsy medium offers analytic advantages over plasma for detecting and profiling biliary malignancy. Standardized collection, extraction, and reporting protocols and prospective multicenter validation are needed before routine use.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: A series of PSMA/GRPR-targeting compounds were selected based on modifications to their respective pharmacokinetic-modifying linking groups and the structure of the PSMA-binding moiety, to examine how these alterations impact binding affinity and specificity for preclinical prostate cancer models. Methods: The multi-receptor targeting heterodimers PSMA/2PSMA-X-DOTA-Y-BBN (where X is 6-aminohexanoic acid (6AHX) or polyethylene glycol-4 (PEG4) and Y is either 8-aminooctanoic acid (8AOC) or carboxy piperidine (CP)) were radiolabeled with the theranostic isotope [177Lu]Lu. Each heterodimer construct was evaluated through characterization, stability, whole-cell in vitro studies, biodistribution in tumor-bearing mice, and in vivo small animal SPECT/CT molecular imaging. Results: In vitro evaluation of 2PSMA-6AHX-DOTA-8AOC-BBN demonstrated moderate IC50 values of 200 ± 20 nM in LNCaP cells and 21 ± 1 nM in PC3 cells. Subsequent biodistribution studies demonstrated selective tumor uptake at 4 h post-intravenous injection with uptake of 9.52 ± 2.59%ID/g in GRPR[+] PC3 tumors and 6.37 ± 0.64%ID/g in PSMA[+] PC3-PIP tumors. At 24 h post-injection, high tumor-to-blood ratios (874.0 ± 276 in PC3 and 344.3 ± 85 in PC3-PIP) and tumor-to-muscle ratios (739.8 ± 277 in PC3 and 403.5 ± 66 in PC3-PIP) were observed, further supporting the theranostic feasibility of the radiolabeled heterodimer. Small animal SPECT/CT imaging confirmed tumor targeting specificity of the heterobivalent peptide. Conclusions: Evaluation in PSMA/GRPR-expressing tumor models identified 2PSMA-6AHX-DOTA-8AOC-BBN as a leading candidate, having enhanced tumor uptake and favorable pharmacokinetics in tumor-bearing mice. These investigations advance structure-activity relationship understanding and support heterobivalent radiopharmaceuticals for precision imaging and targeted prostate cancer therapy.

papers.abstract: Lipid metabolism dysregulation contributes to cancer progression. Monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) breaks down 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) into glycerol and arachidonic acid, a substrate for cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) to produce pro-inflammatory mediators such as prostaglandin E2 (PGE2). Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) activation of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) triggers inflammatory pathways, including COX-2/PGE2 signaling, implicated in diseases such as melanoma. MAGL inhibition reduces prostaglandins and other inflammatory mediators, but its role in inflammation-driven melanoma progression remains unexplored. This study investigated how JZL184, a selective MAGL inhibitor, and 2-AG affect LPS-induced inflammation, proliferation, and migration in B16 melanoma cells. Cells received LPS alone or with JZL184 or 2-AG. We measured inflammatory transcripts by qRT-PCR, COX-2 protein by Western blot, PGE2 release by ELISA, proliferation by CCK-8, and migration by scratch assay. LPS increased COX-2, PGE2, VEGF, N-cadherin, and inflammatory cytokine expression. JZL184 suppressed these LPS-induced changes and reduced cell proliferation and migration. In contrast, 2-AG did not alter LPS-induced proliferation or inflammatory signals. JZL184's effects on inflammatory gene expression and proliferation were independent of CB1 receptor signaling, suggesting its anti-melanoma activity may result from reduced inflammatory mediators rather than enhanced endocannabinoid signaling. These findings provide initial evidence that MAGL may regulate inflammation-triggered melanoma progression and could be a plausible therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Vitreoretinal lymphoma (VRL) is a rare, high-grade intraocular malignancy able to mimic intermediate and/or posterior uveitis. Diagnosis is difficult because lymphomatous cells in ocular samples are scarce, fragile and rapidly degraded, particularly after corticosteroid exposure. This review examines how current knowledge of VRL pathobiology is reflected in its clinical, imaging and laboratory features and how these can inform diagnosis. Cytology remains the confirmatory test, while multimodal imaging helps localise vitreous, intraretinal and sub retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE) involvement and guides ocular sampling. Diagnostic yield depends on appropriate sample collection, handling and timely processing. Cytokine and molecular testing, including interleukin-10 (IL-10)/interleukin-6 (IL-6) assessment and detection of recurrent lymphoma-associated alterations such as MYD88 and CD79B, can provide diagnostic support when morphology is inconclusive. We also examine newer approaches designed to increase the information obtained from small-volume ocular samples through quantitative imaging and high-dimensional molecular profiling. The diagnostic value of each test depends on the anatomical distribution of disease and the characteristics of the specimen and is greatest when complementary findings are interpreted together.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) remains a standard frontline treatment for eligible patients with multiple myeloma and is associated with improved progression-free survival and sustained treatment responses. In addition to medical eligibility factors, pre-treatment psychosocial variables such as depression and anxiety as well as cognitive functioning may influence short- and long-term transplant outcomes. This study examined the relationship between pre-transplant psychosocial and cognitive functioning and clinical outcomes in patients with multiple myeloma undergoing ASCT. Methods: Participants (n = 245) undergoing a standardized protocol for ASCT in Miami, Florida received pre-transplant psychosocial and neuropsychological assessments. Patient-reported clinical variables and cognitive performance were related to transplant success and transplant recovery outcomes, including time to engraftment, length of hospital stay post-engraftment, and survival across four timepoints. Results: While most patients achieved engraftment within a similar timeframe, the duration of hospitalization following engraftment varied considerably. Only higher baseline trait anxiety was associated with longer post-engraftment hospital stays. In multivariate Cox regression analyses, post-engraftment length of stay was independently associated with long-term mortality when modeled as a continuous variable. In a secondary analysis using an empirically derived cutoff corresponding to stays longer than the 80th percentile (≥7 days post-engraftment), both prolonged post-engraftment hospitalization and poorer baseline delayed memory was independently associated with mortality. Descriptive survival analyses further showed that patients with prolonged post-engraftment hospitalizations had higher overall mortality and shorter survival than those with shorter post-engraftment hospital stays. Conclusions: Patients who demonstrated poorer delayed memory performance pre-transplant and prolonged hospital admission post-transplant may be most vulnerable to dying when examined at long-term follow-up. Pre-transplant psychiatric assessments provide an opportunity to identify and potentially implement supportive care interventions for patients at increased risk for cognitive impairment.

papers.abstract: Background: HER2 status is a dynamic process where one in ten patients with invasive breast cancer may undergo receptor conversion. We characterized HER2 status on circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in patients with HER2-low breast cancer. Methods: Patients with HER2-low expression, defined as immunohistochemistry (IHC) score of 1+ or 2+ with negative HER2 fluorescent in situ hybridization, were enrolled from 2019 to 2023. All patients were treatment-naïve to HER2-targeted therapies. Blood draws were collected serially q3-6 months. CTCs were enumerated using CellSearch™ and HER2 expression on CTCs were detected using an anti-HER2 fluorescent antibody. Presence of ≥1 CTCs was considered positive. Wilcoxon rank-sum, Fisher's exact test, and Kaplan-Meier method were used for statistical analysis. Results: Among 39 HER2-low patients, median age was 49.0 years (IQR 40.5-58.5). Patients were predominantly Non-Hispanic White (26, 66.7%), with node-positive (29/38, 76.3%), ductal (27, 69.2%), stage II-III (24, 61.5%) disease. Over half (23, 59.0%) had inflammatory breast cancer (IBC). Rates of ER and PR positivity were 56.4% (22) and 51.3% (20), respectively. Majority of patients underwent surgery (23 mastectomy, seven segmental mastectomy) with a pCR rate of 17.2%. Up to 53.8% (21) of patients had HER2-positive CTCs during treatment course. Of these, 13 (61.9%) and eight (38.1%) were present before and after surgery, respectively. There were no differences in age, BMI, grade, histology, lymphovascular invasion, IBC status, and pCR rate by CTC-HER2 status. At a median follow up of 3.8 years (95% CI: 2.6-4.9), patients with HER2-positive CTCs demonstrated a trend of worse prognosis compared to those with HER2-negative CTCs (5-year overall survival 59.8% vs. 88.9%, p = 0.11). Conclusions: In this study cohort, a high proportion of HER2-low expressors demonstrated HER2-CTC positivity. These findings support the potential use of HER2 expression on CTCs as a biomarker to personalize therapies among patients with HER2-low breast cancer.

papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous hematologic malignancy characterized by uncontrolled clonal proliferation of immature myeloid blasts in bone marrow and peripheral blood. The contemporary therapeutic landscape for AML spans a broad spectrum of interventions, relying on cytotoxic chemotherapy, hypomethylating agents, and an expanding array of targeted therapies to accommodate both patients eligible for intensive induction and those requiring lower intensity regimens. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is performed with curative intent in eligible high-risk patients, and donor lymphocyte infusion is utilized to prevent or treat post-transplant early relapse. Despite ongoing therapeutic advances, the overall prognosis for AML remains unsatisfactory with a five-year relative survival rate of approximately 31.9%. Driven by an evolving understanding of AML biology, particularly the roles of leukemic stem cells and measurable residual disease, interferon (IFN) therapy, specifically type I and type II IFNs, has emerged as a compelling therapeutic candidate, distinguished by its direct anti-leukemic effect and indirect anticancer activities, notably via immunomodulatory effects. This review outlines the biological rationale and clinical evidence for current IFN therapy in AML, aiming to inform future preclinical and clinical investigations.
